title: Entertainment performance robots application in music network classroom based on speech sensor recognition and artificial intelligence
abstract: This article designs a framework for a music online classroom, optimizing the actions of performing robots to improve their performance. Combined with speech recognition and control algorithms, the robot's actions are adjusted in real-time based on the emotions and rhythm of the music to increase student engagement and interactivity. Music recognition adopts methods based on time–frequency analysis and pattern recognition, identifying the type of music played based on the frequency and amplitude distribution patterns in the audio signal; Voice recognition uses feature analysis and speech recognition algorithms based on speech signals to better provide targeted feedback and interaction. This article optimizes the teaching of music online classrooms and verifies the feasibility and effectiveness of using performance robots based on speech sensor recognition and artificial intelligence in music online classrooms through experiments and analysis. Performance robots can mimic the way humans perform music, including singing, playing, and dancing, helping students better understand and imitate music performances. The music online classroom application in this article combines advanced technologies such as voice sensing recognition, artificial intelligence, and performance robots, providing students with a more convenient, personalized, and efficient music learning experience.
keywords: AI plus performance robots | Music online classroom | Speech sensing recognition

title: A novel ensemble machine learning method for accurate air quality prediction
abstract: Air pollution continues to be an important problem that causes health issues worldwide. Factors such as industrial development, increased vehicle traffic, and energy production have a negative impact on air quality by releasing harmful gases and particles into the atmosphere. Consequently, this can lead to respiratory diseases, cardiovascular problems, and other health complications. Predicting air quality is a crucial step in safeguarding human health and informing environmental policies. Many cities employ measurement instruments and data collection systems to monitor and forecast air quality. This data can be analyzed using machine learning models to predict future air pollution levels. This article examines the performance of a new stacking ensemble model for estimating PM<inf>2.5</inf>, based on air quality datasets from major cities such as Beijing and Istanbul. The model combines predictions from various machine learning models. In the initial stage of the study, the performance of commonly used models in the literature, such as multi-layer perceptron, support vector regression, and random forest, were evaluated. These models were assessed for their ability to predict PM<inf>2.5</inf> using metrics such as mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error (RMSE) and R-squared (R<sup>2</sup>). This evaluation determines the proximity of the model predictions to the actual data. The stacking ensemble model examined in this study yielded the best results for PM<inf>2.5</inf> predictions, with MAE of 6.67, RMSE of 8.80 and R<sup>2</sup> of 0.91. In conclusion, the stacking ensemble model for air pollution prediction offers a promising approach for achieving superior results compared to traditional machine learning models.
keywords: Air quality | Ensemble model | Machine learning | Regression

title: Forecasting Commodities Prices Using Machine Learning
abstract: The significance of predicting commodity prices for players in various industries such as agriculture, energy, and finance, allowing them to make rational decisions and minimize risks, cannot be overstated. Although prediction techniques based on traditional models are widely adopted, their efficacy is limited as they tend to lack in capturing the nonlinearities characteristic of the actual commodity markets. Therefore this study delves into the use of machine learning (ML) as a way to predict commodity prices, by taking advantage of its potentiality which is the ability of the computer to analyze large datasets and hence identify hidden relationships. The analysis consists of applying several approaches of supervised learning among which are regression, ensemble methods, and neural networks comparing their aptitude for datasets made up of historical prices, macroeconomic indicators, and external market conditions. Apart from that, there is also a discussion about feature engineering, data preprocessing techniques, and the metrics for measuring a model's performance in order to arrive at reliable predictions. The results have shown that the models based on ML are much more efficient than traditional methods regarding both their accuracy and flexibility, making them a useful instrument for business players. The paper sheds light on how to implement machine learning in practical commodity price prediction scenarios and how it could improve market productivity and decision-making processes.
keywords: Commodity forecasting | data-driven models | machine learning | market analysis | price prediction

title: Improving Piano Notation Transcription in Bisa Aku Bisa Children's Music Using Deep Learning
abstract: This study provides a comparative analysis of manual and AI-Assisted transcription of the children's musical 'Bisa, Aku Bisa'. A basic understanding of manual music notation-especially when learned through instruments like the piano-can help young composers more quickly develop their skills in digital composition using tools such as MuseScore 4 and the music21 Python module. Learning how to arrange music also supports authentic self-expression, helping young composers convey emotions and develop healthy emotional regulation. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence have facilitated the automation of music notation transcription, with deep learning techniques. The research findings indicate that transcription using the music21 python module significantly reduce the time required compared to manual transcription and the use of MuseScore 4. These research results offer valuable insights into the pedagogical application of algorithmic music composition and transcription technologies in children's music education. Moreover, the process of creating children's musical scores by young composers inherently requires a combination of experiential understanding and instrument proficiency. Future research should focus on enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of automated music transcriptions systems, particularly in the context of educational applications and child-focused compositions.
keywords: children's music | deep learning of music composition | piano notation transcription

title: Weighted Ensemble Classification for Misinformation Detection using Optimized TF-IDF Features on a Large-Scale News Dataset
abstract: The swift spread of fake news across digital platforms is really shaking up how people view information and trust in the media. This study rolls out a cutting-edge machine learning framework that works like a team to tell apart real news from fake. It combines the unique strengths of several models: Support Vector Machines (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), Multinomial Naive Bayes (NB), and Gradient Boosting (GB). We've put together a thorough dataset of 44, 898 news articles 21, 417 of which are true and 23, 481 that are fake. To make sense of the text, we preprocess it by tokenizing, removing stopwords, lemmatizing, and using TF-IDF vectorization to pull out key features. We train our individual models on 80% of the data (that's 35, 918 samples), saving the other 20% (8, 980 samples) for testing. By using an ensemble approach, we blend the predictions from these models with optimized weights, which we fine-tune through a grid search to get the best accuracy. An impressive test accuracy of 99.82% is achieved. We dive into detailed evaluations, including classification reports and sample predictions, which show that our model holds up well across various types of news content. Our results highlight how effective ensemble learning can be for detecting fake news, providing a reliable and scalable solution for automated content verification - perfect for media monitoring and social media platforms. We also pinpoint some areas that could use improvement, like tackling the stylistic similarities between true and fake news, setting the stage for future research into better feature engineering and model designs.
keywords: Ensemble Learning | Fake News Detection | Logistic Regression | Machine Learning | Naive Bayes | SVM

title: INVOX: A Robust System For Detecting Synthetic Voice Attacks
abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI), especially in Text-to-Speech (TTS) and Voice Conversion (VC) technologies, has greatly enhanced the quality of voice-driven applications while also increasing vulnerability to synthetic voice attacks. This paper introduces Invox, an explainable deep learning framework aimed at ensuring reliable detection and characterization of AI-generated spoofed speech. The framework incorporates log-mel spectrogram preprocessing, a hybrid CNN - Transformer architecture for hierarchical feature representation, and an ensemble decision model that merges CNN-BiLSTM, SVM, and GBDT classifiers. Additionally, InVox presents a Voice Authenticity Score, detailed spoof-type categorization, and attention-driven visual interpretability to facilitate forensic analysis and promote transparent decision-making. By combining robust modeling with explainable outputs, InVox provides a practical and secure foundation for implementation in banking, customer service, and high-assurance voice authentication settings.
keywords: CNN | Deepfake audio | Ensemble learning | Explainable AI | Synthetic speech detection | Transformer

title: Deep Ensemble Emotion Recognition from Speech Using YOLO Feature Extraction and RF+ADABoost Classification
abstract: Emotion recognition through speech has proven to be an important aspect of developing human-computer interaction systems that will be empathetic. Conventional methods use manually designed feature and distinct modules to extract features and classify them which in many cases leads to less than optimal performance. The study presents a completely end-to-end deep learning system which learns discriminative audio representations using raw speech signals. A YOLO Ensemble is used as a feature extractor in the proposed system to extract salient patterns of time and spectral features within speech. These are then fed through a hybrid ensemble classifier with the combination of Random Forest (RF) and AdaBoost which is known as RFADABoost that improves the strength of classification with complementary decision boundaries and adaptive weighting. Unlike traditional CNN-LSTM models that need to process data in a specific order (like a sequence), this architecture doesn't rely on that. Instead, it uses ensemble learning, which is good at handling complex, high-dimensional data without needing to follow a strict sequence. When compared to the conventional classifiers Decision Tree and Naive Bayes, it can be seen that YOLO+RFADABoost performs much better, as it was able to reach 96% accuracy, which confirms that the algorithm is efficient in emotion recognition in speech.
keywords: AdaBoost | CNN+LSTM | Decision Tree | NaiveBayes | RF | Speech recognition | YOLO

title: Predicting Music Origin with Deep Learning
abstract: This study explores the use of deep learning to predict the geographic origin of music based on audio features. Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs) were extracted to capture acoustic information, while language was identified using OpenAI's Whisper model to provide additional contextual signals. A late fusion neural network architecture combining Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layers for sequential MFCC input and dense layers for non-sequential language features were employed to support both classification and regression tasks. The classification model achieved an accuracy of 33.03% across 56 countries and territories, substantially outperforming the uniform random baseline (1.79%), the prior-weighted random baseline (3.59%), and andom Forest baseline (9.1%). The regression model produced a Mean Great-Circle Error (MGCE) of 2,754.83km. While regression offers more flexibility for geographic estimation, classification demonstrated a more promising performance with the current dataset. This work highlights the potential of multimodal learning in music-origin prediction.
keywords: deep learning | geographic classification | LSTM | MFCC | MIR | Multimodal learning

title: Developing A Multi-Disease Risk Prediction Model Using Machine Learning
abstract: The ability to predict the risk of multiple diseases accurately is a crucial step toward improving early diagnosis and healthcare outcomes. With the potential to improve and automate the diagnostic procedure, machine learning methods have become more effective instruments for this aim in recent years. This study focuses on developing a machine learning model to predict the risk of different diseases by using Transfer Learning, where pre-trained models are used to enhance the prediction accuracy. A comparison was done of three models, namely, Transfer Learning (proposed model), VGG-16, and DenseNet-121, in the multi-disease risk prediction context. The proposed Transfer Learning model reached a maximum accuracy of 98.3%, which is higher than the VGG-16 at 94% and DenseNet-121 at 92% in key evaluation metrics, such as precision, recall, and F1-score. This demonstrated how Transfer Learning could produce more balanced and accurate predictions of a variety of diseases, including influenza, asthma, diabetes, heart attacks, and many others. The findings provide evidence that Transfer Learning can indeed be applied to real-world health care scenarios, and it thus offers a very promising tool in the early prediction of disease. Future work will include fine-tuning the model, dealing with class imbalances in health datasets, and ensemble learning to enhance the model even further. Ultimately, this may then allow for an efficient deployment of machine learning models in clinical settings to improve disease diagnosis and manage risks.
keywords: Deep Learning | Disease Diagnosis | Healthcare Applications | Machine Learning | Model Optimizati...

title: A Hybrid AI-Powered Framework for Accurate Urban Flood Prediction and Real-Time Early Warning Systems
abstract: Urban flooding presents increasing threats to densely populated cities as a result of climate change and urbanisation. Current flood prediction models often show deficiencies in real-time accuracy and do not deliver timely notifications, hence constraining disaster preparedness. This proposed study presents a hybrid AI system that combines Gradient Boosted Decision Trees with a CNN-BiLSTM ensemble to analyse spatial-temporal patterns from different datasets. The system, employing rainfall and water-level data from Kaggle, attains exceptional performance metrics: 97.83% accuracy, 98.15% recall, and an AUC-ROC of 0.993, markedly exceeding baseline models such as Random Forest and LSTM. The framework's real-time alarm distribution improves responsiveness, potentially minimising flood-related damages and fatalities. This methodology enhances flood prediction through the integration of explainability, accuracy, and operational security, providing it an essential instrument for urban disaster management.
keywords: BiLSTM | CNN | Disaster Management | Flood Risk Assessment | Gradient Boosted Decision Trees | Hy...

title: Multimodal Emotion Recognition Using Acoustic Features and Deep Language Models
abstract: Emotion recognition makes it possible for systems to respond to users in natural and commiserative ways, emotion recognition is so necessary part of affective computing. To classify emotions more precisely, in this study a framework was devised, including text and voice data. For the audio part, we relied on MFCC based representations (9,793 samples) and popu- lar databases EMO-DB (535 samples) and IEMOCAP (10,190 samples). This involves feeling both at high, low, and neutral levels of intensity excitement frustration and anger sadness etc. We explored models including stacking, multilayer perceptron, voting ensembles and XGBoost with data such as pitch, loudness, MFCCs and chroma. They ranged in accuracy from 39 percent to 45 percent. We used 5,427 labeled samples for 28 fine-grained emotions such as pride, remorse. appreciation, curiosity and admiration for the text modality. We analyzed the transcribed text after performing speech-to-text using BERT and BiLSTM. The text-based models - at nearly a 95% accuracy rate - were better than the audio-only ones. Even back then, we were insulated from relying on any one source. Instead, we combined the-textual and speech-predictions. This stage felt logical since each had its contribution to make: the words themselves would clarify what was said, while the voice would convey how it was presented. Together this gave us a solid base to work from in terms of a consistent, balanced product. The audio signals have value and can pair with text to provide information that allows systems to recognize emotions.
keywords: Affective Computing | and Speech Processing | Audio Features | BERT | BiLSTM | Emotion Recognitio...

title: MuGen-100: A Diverse and Geographically-Rich Dataset for Music Genre Classification
abstract: In our paper we explore Music genre classification and more precisely the datasets used for that. We noticed that the available datasets used for experiments and research and sometimes even deployed products, there is often a limited cultural perspective [1]. To help this field toward more inclusive and culturally-aware machine learning models, we introduce MuGen-100: A dataset of 100 genres curated from different areas and places of the world. We hope to provide the public with a benchmark resource that provides cultural richness and offers practical and flexible utility. We will also share some baseline performance results to showcase MuGen's potential and how it could be further extended and enhanced in future works.
keywords: Audio deep learning | CNN | Cultural diversity in machine learning | Dataset | Music genre classi...

title: Hierarchical BiLSTM Encoding for Vocal-Driven Cover Song Detection
abstract: Cover song detection remains a challenging task due to significant variations in key, tempo, timbre, and arrangement across different versions of the same song. In this paper, we propose a deep learning neural net that leverages isolated vocal stems and extracts multiple complementary low-level beat synchronized audio features - MFCC, Chroma and CQT. These features are processed through a multi-branch BiLSTM-Attention architecture designed to generate musically discriminative embeddings. We use triplet focal loss in training process.The unique combination of BiLSTM and hierarchical sparse attention mechanism improves the embedding separability. Experiments on the SHS100K dataset demonstrate good retrieval performance, achieving a MAP @ 10 of 0.713 and an MRI of 23.7.
keywords: Attention Mechanisms | Cover Song Detection | Deep Metric Learning | Embedding | Music Informatio...

title: USAD: Universal Speech and Audio Representation via Distillation
abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) has revolutionized audio representations, yet models often remain domain-specific, focusing on either speech or non-speech tasks. In this work, we present Universal Speech and Audio Distillation (USAD), a unified approach to audio representation learning that integrates diverse audio types - speech, sound, and music - into a single model. USAD employs efficient layer-to-layer distillation from domain-specific SSL models to train a student on a comprehensive audio dataset. USAD offers competitive performance across various benchmarks and datasets, including frame and instance-level speech processing tasks, audio tagging, and sound classification, achieving near state-of-the-art results with a single encoder on SUPERB and HEAR benchmarks.<sup>1</sup>Models: https://huggingface.co/MIT-SLS/USAD-Base
keywords: knowledge distillation | self-supervised learning | speech and audio representation learning

title: Machine Learning Framework for Audio-Based Equipment Condition Monitoring: A Comparative Study of Classification Algorithms
abstract: Audio-based equipment condition monitoring suffers from a lack of standardized methodologies for algorithm selection, hindering reproducible research. This paper addresses this gap by introducing a comprehensive framework for the systematic and statistically rigorous evaluation of machine learning models. Leveraging a rich 127-feature set across time, frequency, and time-frequency domains, our methodology is validated on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Results demonstrate that an ensemble method achieves superior performance (94.2% accuracy, 0.942 F1-score), with statistical testing confirming its significant outperformance of individual algorithms by 8-15%. Ultimately, this work provides a validated benchmarking protocol and practical guidelines for selecting robust monitoring solutions in industrial settings.
keywords: algorithm comparison | audio signal processing | condition monitoring | ensemble methods | fault ...

title: Integrating Physiological Signals into Music Machine Learning: An HRV-Based Framework
abstract: Music is widely being recognized as a non-pharmacological intervention for anxiety, yet its physiological mechanisms remain unexplored. This study examines the effect of Kaapi raga (a south Indian classical music) and weightless ambient music on cardiovascular regulation and anxiety reduction using heart rate variability (HRV) and mean arterial pressure (MAP). Twenty participants with high anxiety (HAM-A >25) completed a protocol involving rest, music listening, and attention tasks while ECG and MAP were continuously recorded.HRV features were extracted across time, frequency, and nonlinear domains and analysed using machine learning classifiers. Random Forest and XGBoost achieved the highest performance (70.8% accuracy; AUC up to 0.89), outperforming linear models. Feature ablation revealed non-linear SD2, pNN50, HR mean, and high-frequency power percentage as key predictors of music-induced physiological changes.The findings here demonstrate that ensemble machine learning methods can robustly model music's impact on anxiety, while domain-specific HRV features provide actionable biomarkers for developing personalized, evidence-based music therapy interventions.
keywords: Feature Ablation | Heart Rate Variability | Machine learning | Music

title: Automated Detection of Diabetic Macular Edema Using Deep Learning on Fundus Images
abstract: The severe diabetic retinopathy complication known as Diabetic Macular Edema (DME) leads to the most common vision loss form in diabetic patients. Automated screening identification of DME in an early stage represents an effective way to prevent complete vision damage. Unlike existing systems, an ensemble deep learning detection system along with Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM), a visualizing technique to display the most important image regions for finding DME is introduced in this study. Additionally, a performance comparison of DenseNet121, EfficientNetB3, ResNet50V2 along with InceptionV3 methods for DME has been done. his study utilized the Messidor-2 dataset comprising 1,748 color fundus images with a resolution of 1 4 4 0 × 9 6 0 pixels. High diagnostic capability for DME detection emerges from the developed model which produces 0.946 AUC and simultaneous sensitivity of 94.1% and specificity of 79.6%. The results clearly demonstrate that the ensemble approach proposed in this study outperforms the individual models while delivering a reliable screening instrument which matches well between sensitivity and specificity for clinical DME screening applications. Unlike prior studies using isolated CNN architectures, this work introduces a weighted ensemble framework combining DenseNet121, EfficientNetB3, ResNet50V2, and InceptionV3 for more reliable DME screening. The integration of Grad-CAM provides transparent visualization of clinically relevant retinal regions. The study utilizes the Messidor-2 dataset containing 1,748 fundus images (1440 × 960 px), with a 70: 15: 15 training-validation-test split and a9:91 DME-positive to negative ratio, ensuring reproducibility and robustness.
keywords: Computer-Aided Diagnosis | Deep Learning | Diabetic Macular Edema | Ensemble Learning | Fundus Im...

title: Optimizing Network Security Protocols with Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM) in Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: This research aims to analyze how Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM) can enhance network security in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). Considering the fact that WSNs are resource-constrained and are susceptible to security threats, doesn't allow the application of conventional security methods. To accomplish this, the present study proposes the implementation of GBM, a potent ensemble learning procedure, in order to improve the reliability of various security mechanisms in WSNs. The plan is to collect the corresponding data, preprocess it, train a machine learning model, and, finally, implement it in the network in real-time. The use of the GBM model yielded better results than the baseline methods, given high accuracy, precision, and recall rates in analyzing security threats. The study shows that utilization of GBM can enhance the security of WSNs by up to 50%, and thus GBM can be used as an instrument to prevent WSNs in various vital applications, supporting the principles of Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) for promoting sustainable innovation and resilient infrastructure in digital communication systems.
keywords: Ensemble learning | Gradient Boosting Machines | Network Security | SDG | Sustainable Innovation ...

title: Application of the Cascade Method in the Integration of Whisper and Ensemble NLP for Speech Summarization
abstract: In the era of information overload and due to declined human cognitive skill, efficient comprehension of spoken content has become increasingly important. This study propose a cascade-based speech summarization framework that integrates OpenAI’s Whisper-small model for speech recognition and Ensemble Model that combine T5, Pegasus, and BART for abstractive text summarization process. The CNN/DailyMail News dataset is used for the training and evaluation process. The system aims to transform spoken input into concise, semantically coherent summaries while minimizing transcription and summarizations errors. The methodology consists of two sequential stages, which are Whisper-based ASR for transcription and ensemble model summarization using reranking method. Experimental results demonstrate that Whisper-small achieved an exceptional transcription accuracy with WER of 3.3% and CER of 1.7%. Among individual models, BART obtained the highest summarization performance with ROUGE-L of 0.7498, while the ensemble model achieved balanced performance across all metrics.
keywords: Deep Learning | Ensemble Model | NLP | Speech Summarization | Whisper

title: A Weighted Ensemble of Multi-Scale Fusion CNNs for Melanoma Classification
abstract: The early and accurate diagnosis of malignant melanoma remains a significant challenge in dermatology, largely due to the high visual similarity between malignant and benign skin lesions. This paper introduces a novel classification methodology tested on the challenging and highly imbalanced ISIC 2017 dataset. A custom multi-scale feature fusion head was designed to improve the feature extraction capabilities of standard Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) backbones. Through systematic evaluation, an EfficientNetB6 model equipped with this fusion head was identified as the most effective single-model architecture. To further boost the performance, a weighted ensemble was developed that combines the outputs of our two best fusion models: EfficientNetB6 and DenseNet201. The final proposed model, utilizing a 90/10 weighting scheme, achieved an F1-score of 0.5517, an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.8174, and a clinically significant recall of 75.2%. The experimental results demonstrated that this weighted ensemble of multi-scale fusion models offers a superior balance between precision and recall, establishing an effective strategy for this complex classification task.
keywords: Computer-Aided Diagnosis | Deep Learning | Ensemble Learning | ISIC 2017 | Melanoma Classificatio...

title: Improving Sentiment Classification Accuracy using Engagement and Temporal Features from Social Media Data
abstract: Sentiment analysis has become an important instrument to gain insight on user attitudes, brands and trends in online behavior and digital platforms. This paper addresses this aspect by conducting a recognizable study of an approach encompassing all the available methodologies on classifying sentiment in three categories, i.e. positive, negative and neutral as well as traditional Machine Learning (ML) models, ensemble approaches and a stacking-based combination approach. Different independent classifier models such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), Naive Bayes (NB) mode have been tested with Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) features on a sentiment dataset that has undergone preprocessing. Hard voting and extended voting using multiple learners are applied to make a more significant improvement in performance. It shows the biggest benefit in a stacking ensemble model, where LR, NB and SVM are implemented as base learners, and Random Forest (RF) serves as a meta-learner. The findings confirm the usefulness of using hybrid ensemble models in sentiment classification particularly when sparse and moderate sized data sets are involved.
keywords: Brand Management | Machine Learning | Natural Language Processing | Sentimental Analysis | Social...

title: Enhancing Stock Price Forecasts with Random Forests and Simple Moving Average Indicators
abstract: Accurate stock price forecasting is known to be a challenging problem for financial markets, since the stock price has a volatile and nonlinear nature. This paper conducts a systematic comparison of two machine learning tools, namely, Support Vector Regression (SVR) and Random Forest Regression (RFR), for predicting the next-day adjusted closing prices of stocks. Both models are trained on a simple yet powerful feature set: adjusted close, 5-day and 10-day SMA, and are fitted to historical stock data. The assessment is carried out on two performance metrics: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and the coefficient of determination (R<sup>2).</sup> Results obtained from a wide range of shares show that Random Forest consistently outperforms with larger average R<sup>2</sup> and smaller RMSE values across the board. Although SVR achieves good results in smoother and more stationary trends, it is sensitive to noisy trends and parameter configurations. The ensemble nature of Random Forest is more robust and suitable for capturing complex market behaviors. This comparative study highlights the efficiency of ensemble-based models in financial forecasting.
keywords: Predictive Modeling | Random Forest | Simple Moving Averages | Stock Price Forecasting | Support ...

title: Advancing Earthquake Prediction Accuracy Through Machine Learning: A GBM-Based Study on Diagnostic Performance and Reliability
abstract: In the study of seismic data, earthquake prediction has proved to be an important issue because of the sophisticated, non-linear, character of the information. In this paper, we discuss the effectiveness of Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM), a strong ensemble learning algorithm, in classifying earthquake events over a well-organized seismic data set. We used stratified data partitions to train and validate our model, which would result in the balancing and confirm appropriate representation of classes. This analysis was done by using various performance measurements and illustrations in order to carry out an effective evaluation. The Confusion matrix indicates a high level of classification of the model, with true positive number of 358 and true negative number of 288, and false negative 34, and false positive 85. The combined accuracy is at 84 percent implying a balanced sensitivity on the model with regard to earthquake and non-earthquake cases. Also, the precision of non-earthquake and earthquake are 0.89 and 0.81 respectively in the classification report whereas recall is high in earthquake cases (0.91) which means high sensitivity and less chance of misses. The high values of the F1-score (0.83 and 0.86, respectively) indicate overall high balance between the precision and recall in classes 0 and 1. The Discriminative strength of the model is further supported by Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve which indicates a good ability to discriminate between the 2 classes with Area under the curve (AUC) score of 0.90. In the learning curve results, training and validation scores improve steadily and converge at the end of the learning curve, and threshold analysis proves that the model is optimized by avoiding either false positive or false negative. This method which is based on GBM shows quite high level of accuracy and strength in earthquake prediction. Due to its capacity to run complicated seismic characteristics, it is being utilized as an invaluable instrument in disaster preparedness, in combination with early warning systems, which portrays a data-based approach to the kind of reliability that results in seismic event predictions.
keywords: Diagnostic Accuracy | Earthquake Prediction | Gradient Boosting Machine | Machine Learning | Seis...

title: A GeneSwarm-Enhanced Hybrid Ensemble Model for Predicting Cardiac Outcomes in Kawasaki Disease
abstract: Kawasaki Disease (KD) is a paediatric vasculitis that may cause coronary artery lesions (CAL) in case it is not diagnosed and treated early. The problem of complicated clinical data and nonspecific markers has complicated proper forecasting of the long-term KD outcomes. This paper suggests a hybrid ensemble machine learning model to use XGBoost, AdaBoost, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers and soft voting in order to have robust and interpretable predictions. The GeneSwarm Feature Selector was used to select the features based on the Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization which can optimally identify the most informative and non-redundant clinical and laboratory features. The Babysitting algorithm was used to optimize hyperparameters dynamically and Interquartile Range (IQR) to eliminate outliers and Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to deal with class imbalance were used during preprocessing. Assessed on 1,850 paediatric KD cases, the proposed model demonstrated a 97.10% accuracy, 96.50% precision, 96.80% recall, 96.60% F1-score, and a macro-AUC of 97.40% and is better than the current ML methods. Best predictive variables were Complications, Clinical Outcomes, Treatment Approach, Echocardiography, Laboratory Tests, Fever Duration, and Symptoms. These findings indicate that the framework is a reliable, interpretable, and clinically applicable instrument of early KD prognosis, which helps to plan personalized treatment and stratify risks. Through the incorporation of superior feature selection, ensemble learning, and a solid preprocessing, the research will add to an empirical and pragmatic method of enhancing cardiac care in pediatrics.
keywords: Babysitting Algorithm | Feature Selection | GeneSwarm | Hybrid Ensemble | Kawasaki Disease | Mach...

title: Hybrid Ensemble Machine Learning Framework for Predictive Consumer Food Safety Risk Assessment
abstract: Food safety is still a global public health issue. Every year, more than 600 million people get sick from foodborne illnesses because of unsafe handling, bad vendor practices, and not enough predictive surveillance. Current studies reveal substantial discrepancies between consumer and vendor knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) and actual contamination outcomes, especially in low- and middle-income nations. To mitigate these constraints, this study introduces an innovative Machine Learning-Driven Framework for Safeguarding Consumer Food Safety, amalgamating behavioral, environmental, and microbiological data into a cohesive predictive model. The suggested system uses hybrid ensemble learning, which combines Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Support Vector Machines, to figure out the risk of contamination and sort hazards into different levels. A dataset comprising 10,000 consumer-vendor interactions and 1,200 microbiological samples was subjected to a 10-fold cross-validation protocol for analysis. The model had an accuracy of 94.6%, an F1-score of 0.93, and an AUC of 0.96 (p < 0.001), which was 8.4% better than baseline models. An analysis of feature importance showed that vendor hygiene compliance, food temperature, and consumer awareness were the most important factors. SHAP-based feature attribution made sure that the model was explainable, which made it easier to understand for policy and regulatory use. The proposed framework offers a scalable, privacy-preserving instrument for early contamination forecasting and evidence-based intervention formulation. Future extensions will investigate federated learning and IoT integration to facilitate real-time monitoring and adaptive risk management in various food systems.
keywords: Consumer Protection | Explainable AI | Food Safety | Machine Learning | Public Health | Risk Pred...

title: Identifying Fake Audio Using Social Media Metadata and Audio Features
abstract: With a rise in AI generated audio, more commonly referred to as audio deepfakes, it has become increasingly important to detect fake audio content especially as it spreads across social media. While most detection methods rely only on analyzing the sound itself, they often miss important clues found in social media engagement data. In this work, we introduce a new approach that combines both audio features (such as, spectrograms, energy levels, tempo, and pitch-related measurements) and social media metadata (such as likes, dislikes, and comment counts) to determine whether an audio clip is real, or AI generated. We developed an ensemble model that brings together five different machine learning methods being, Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, and a Neural Network which uses a stacking approach to improve overall prediction. We compared the results acquired from this model to the results of well known papers, including CFAD, Singfake, and ASVspoof 2019. Our model achieved an AUC of 0.847, accuracy of 84.6%, and an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 20.4%, showing that it performs similarly, if not better, than existing methods that use only audio. These results suggest that combining sound with social context offers a promising and practical way to detect deepfake audio, especially in a real world social media setting. While our model achieved moderate performance (AUC of 0.847), it highlights the potential and limitations of combining social and audio features in deepfake audio detection, and opens avenues for future tuning and dataset expansion.
keywords: Artificial Intelligence | Audio Detection | Binary Classification | DeepFakes | Ensemble Learning...

title: Randomized Neural Network with Multiple Output Layers for Multi-label Classification
abstract: Multi-label classification (MLC) applications span numerous real-world domains, including music annotation, medical diagnosis, and biological analysis, where instances may be associated with multiple categories simultaneously. However, MLC is a challenging problem due to imbalanced label distributions that exist in multi-label data, making accurate prediction more complicated. In this paper, we propose a Multi-Label ensemble deep Random Vector Functional Link (ML-edRVFL) framework that extends the edRVFL architecture with multiple output layers to multi-label setting by integrating three adaptive thresholding techniques and two ensemble aggregation rules. The framework is evaluated on four benchmark datasets from diverse domains. The experimental results show that the proposed ML-edRVFL models achieve competitive performance in comparison to the baseline methods.

title: AQGSM: Efficient Multimodal AVQA via Ensemble Transformer Optimization
abstract: Audio-Visual Question Answering (AVQA) requires reasoning across the interdependencies of the audio and visual modalities, therefore, making the task more challenging than the traditional Visual Question Answering (VQA). Current architectures such as the Collective QuestionGuided Network (CQGN) can perform well on benchmark tasks such as MUSICAVQA; however, these systems are hindered by redundancy in question generation and large computation costs. In response to the short-comings, we propose an augmented CQGN architecture with an Adaptive Question Generation and Selection Module (AQGSM). It is a module that applies an ensemble of transformer encoders, namely, DeBERTa-v3-base, RoBERTa-base, ELECTRA-base, and BERT-base, with the weight of 0.28, 0.25, 0.24, and 0.23 respectively, to make use of context-sensitive question generation and selection.Image representations are acquired through the CLIP ViT-B/32 encoder, whereas audio representations are acquired through Wav2Vec 2.0, and the two modalities are then combined in a multimodal integration component.With a systematic hyperparameter search on a 45,000 instance AVQA corpus, the weighted ensemble accuracy is 93.24 percentage on the validation split, and the expected performance can be improved to 94.7 percent with additional optimization. Additionally, the architecture has lowered inference time to 0.65s/batch.These findings imply an improved efficiency, scalability, and usability over baseline systems like CQGN (77 per cent accuracy) and the MAV-LLM/LAVA pipelines.
keywords: Adaptive Question Generation | Audio-Visual Question Answering (AVQA) | BERT | DeBERTa-v3 | ELECT...

title: Student Depression Prediction: A Multimodal Machine Learning Approach
abstract: In today's world, Depression among students has been a critical mental health concern that substantially impacts desired outcomes, productivity, and overall human well-being. Traditional diagnostic instruments involve conventional medical tools, classical diagnostic apparatus, or conventional diagnostic equipment such as the PHQ-9 questionnaire provide effective clinical measures but lack of ease of use in digital-first environments. This paper put forward a plan for multimedia machine learning (ML) framework that integrates behavioral features (mobility, smartphone usage, sleeping patterns) and other feature like linguistics features (related to language text contents from essays and posts on social medias) to estimate depression. A dataset of 820 university students was taken and compared with PHQ-9 scores as ground truth labels. Hereby the functioning of models including BERT, RoBERT, Random Forest, Logistic Regression and a Fusion Ensemble was evaluated. Outcomes show that the fusion approach outperforms unimodal baselines, which brings to a successful conclusion with a veracity of 86% and and of 0.91. Thereafter we give out interpretability results using SHAP, drawing attention to the most influential predictors of depression.
keywords: BERT | KEY PHRASES- Student depression | machine learning | multimodal learning | PHQ-9 | RoBERTa...

title: Chroma Features Based Music Genre Classification Using Machine and Deep Learning Algorithms
abstract: This study investigates the efficacy of various machine learning and deep learning models for automated music genre classification. Utilizing the GTZAN dataset, a comprehensive collection of audio features was extracted and preprocessed, including Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), Chroma features, Spectral Centroid, Root Mean Square (RMS), and Spectral Bandwidth. The dataset, comprising 3-second audio segments, was used to train and evaluate K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Classifier (SVC), Decision Tree, Random Forest, and a custom-built Deep Neural Network (DNN). A comparative analysis of model performance, supported by accuracy metrics and confusion matrices, reveals the strengths and limitations of each approach in distinguishing between ten distinct music genres. The findings underscore the importance of robust feature engineering and appropriate model selection for accurate Music Information Retrieval (MIR) tasks, highlighting areas were acoustic similarities challenge classification algorithms.
keywords: Chroma Features | Deep Neural Network | GTZAN | Music Genre Classification | Music Information Re...

title: Automatic Beatmap Generation in Web-Based Rhythm Games: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Rhythm games rely on beatmaps that translate music into interactive visual and timing patterns. Manual beatmap creation is labor-intensive and requires expert knowledge, prompting research into automatic beatmap generation (ABG) to improve scalability and accessibility. This paper presents a systematic literature review (SLR) of 21 studies concerning ABG with an emphasis on web-based deployment. The review identifies the main objectives of prior systems, reducing authoring time, maintaining playability, and supporting educational or cultural purposes. It also summarizes the user-experience (UX) features and algorithmic techniques employed, including rule-based, signal-processing, data-driven, and hybrid models. Efficiency factors such as latency, runtime performance, and browser compatibility are analyzed to evaluate feasibility for real-time interaction on heterogeneous devices. Findings indicate that lightweight and constraint-aware approaches, when combined with optimized deep-learning inference, can achieve human-like playability in browser environments. The study concludes with research directions toward standardized datasets, web-native evaluation benchmarks, and broader integration of traditional and folk-music repertoires in rhythm-game applications.
keywords: automatic beatmap generation | music information retrieval | rhythm games | systematic literature...

title: Ta Ka Di Mi: AI for Konnakkol and Rhythm Training
abstract: We present Ta Ka Di Mi, an AI-powered mobile application designed to make rhythm training and Konnakkol-the South Indian art of vocal percussion-accessible to learners worldwide. Konnakkol is a centuries-old tradition where rhythmic syllables are recited to convey complex tala (time cycles or rhythmic frameworks), often serving as both a pedagogical tool and a performance art. While deeply rooted in South Indian classical music, rhythm itself is a universal language, integral to music, dance, speech, and movement across cultures. Despite this universality, learning Konnakkol has traditionally required close mentorship, consistent practice, and significant exposure to expert practitioners, making it less accessible outside specialized communities. Our system addresses these challenges by combining modern AI technologies with carefully curated pedagogical content to create an interactive, scalable, and user-friendly learning experience for global audiences. The application integrates automatic speech recognition, audio signal processing, and real-time feedback models to evaluate learners across multiple dimensions: rhythmic accuracy, pronunciation fidelity, and tempo consistency. Through gamified lessons, learners can progress from foundational exercises to advanced rhythmic improvisations, guided by structured modules designed in collaboration with renowned artist B.C. Manjunath. The AI-driven evaluation engine provides instant personalized feedback, enabling learners to refine their skills iteratively and at their own pace. In addition, the app incorporates adaptive learning strategies that track a user's growth over time and dynamically suggest exercises tailored to individual strengths and weaknesses. Our demo highlights the unique intersection of cultural heritage and modern AI, showcasing how domain-specific AI/ML techniques can be applied to music education in a globally meaningful way. Beyond traditional music training, Ta Ka Di Mi supports diverse use cases, including rhythm practice for dancers and instrumentalists, therapeutic interventions for speech and motor coordination, and cross-cultural exploration for learners worldwide who seek rhythm as a bridge across traditions. By blending ancient tradition with contemporary technology, the platform not only preserves and disseminates an important cultural practice but also reimagines how rhythm can be taught, experienced, and shared universally. Ultimately, Ta Ka Di Mi demonstrates how AI can democratize access to art forms, enhance pedagogy through personalized insights, and foster global community-building around rhythm. In bridging the gap between ancient tradition and modern technology, the system illustrates the potential of AI-powered education platforms to enrich cultural learning and inspire new creative possibilities across the world. A short demo video is available at: https://youtu.be/LveumJymJ-M.

title: Predictive Modelling for Oral Cancer Detection using Machine Learning
abstract: Oral cancer (OC) remains a significant free strength tricky, and primary finding is critical to improving patient outcomes. The research will create multiple ML models to determine OC prediction possibilities based on clinical and demographic information. The data processing phase used label encoding followed by scaling then filled in any absent values in the patient information database. The study evaluated five machine learning (ML) classifiers through training and assessment of Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost and LightGBM as well as Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Logistic Regression (LR). Among them, The XGBoost model produced the best performance with 0.92 ROC AUC score while RF obtained 0.89 and LightGBM demonstrated 0.88. The F1 scores together with the accuracy values varied from 0.80 to 0.90 across evaluated models. Research findings indicate ensemble-based tools especially XGBoost present great potential as diagnostic instruments which help detect oral cancer in its early stages.
keywords: Hybrid Model | Machine Learning | Oral Cancer | Random Forest | Support Vector Machine

title: Toward Early Detection of Prediabetes in Children: A Multimodal Analysis of Oral, Cutaneous, and Metabolic Indicators
abstract: Early detection of pre-diabetes in children and adolescents is essential to prevent its progression to type-2 diabetes. In paediatric settings, conventional diagnostic approaches relying on invasive blood tests often pose practical and psychological challenges. This study investigates the feasibility of using external physiological indicators, specifically tongue and skin features, as non-invasive markers of early metabolic alteration. To support this objective, a tri-modal screening framework integrating clinical parameters with machine-learning-based image analysis is proposed to enable patient-friendly assessment. The dataset comprises 127 synthetically generated clinical image cases, with a mean participant age of 14.13 years. From these images, a total of 152 quantitative features were extracted, including GLCM-based texture metrics, colour-distribution descriptors, and high-dimensional deep-learning representations. These visual features were analysed alongside metabolic indices such as HbA1c and fasting blood glucose. The ensemble model that combined all modalities achieved an area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.94, with a sensitivity of 92% and specificity of 88%, demonstrating strong diagnostic potential. Overall, the findings support the use of visual cues as a viable, non-invasive approach for early pre-diabetes screening in paediatric populations. Validation on larger, real-world, and demographically diverse cohorts will be essential for future clinical adoption.
keywords: image analysis | machine learning | metabolic markers | non-invasive diagnosis | paediatric scree...

title: Music Popularity Prediction Platform
abstract: Predicting the popularity of songs has long been a challenge in the music industry due to rapidly changing listener preferences and evolving production practices. This is an empirical study with a deployed prototype. It applies machine learning techniques to audio features and temporal metadata spanning six decades of music to predict whether a track will achieve commercial popularity. Four models were developed and evaluated, including a tuned Random Forest with decade encoding, which demonstrated superior performance in terms of F1-score and ROC-AUC. Stratified sampling and per-decade validation ensured robustness against temporal bias, while feature importance analyses revealed danceability, instrumentalness, and acousticness as key predictors. SHAP-based explainability methods provided transparency into model decisions, enhancing trust and interpretability. A Streamlit-based application was also deployed to offer an interactive interface for exploring predictions, enabling threshold tuning and scenario testing. Results suggest that integrating temporal context with acoustic features improves predictive accuracy and provides actionable insights for playlist curation, artist scouting, and trend forecasting. The platform's ranking, calibration, and explainability support practical Artist scouting, repertoire triage and playlist curation, offering measurable screening efficiency and transparent decision support for labels and distributors
keywords: Acoustic Features | API | CRISP-DM | Feature Engineering | Interpretability | Machine Learning | ...

title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Cryptocurrency Trend Prediction via Candlestick Charts and Technical Indicators
abstract: The growth of Bitcoin cryptocurrency with large fluctuations has aroused the interest of large investors, leading to the need for institutional investors to be at the forefront of short-term cryptocurrency trend prediction technology. To address the complexities caused by nonlinearity, this paper proposes a fusion model combining the MobileNetV2 model to capture candlestick chart morphology, OHLCV series with technical indicators modeled by GRU for short-term dependencies, and nonautoregressive encoder (NAR) to extract long-term context. Then, the features of each model are merged into the XGBoost model for classification (Bull/Bear/Neutral), which is mapped into trading signals while integrating the Uncertainty gating decision mechanism to increase reliability. Using the 15minute BTC/USDT dataset from Binance, divided into 70%/15%/15% ensembles, the merged model achieved an accuracy of 74.3 %, macro-F1 of 0.7429, and MCC of 0.4867, outperforming the single-method and baseline methods. The trust-aware gating results further improved the reliability, raising the accuracy and F1 to over 81% with a coverage of 67.74%, with a high threshold exceeding 98% accuracy for selective predictions. The above results demonstrate that the combination of multi-methods with the Uncertainty gating decision mechanism provides a reliable and practical forecasting tool for the volatile cryptocurrency market.

title: Enhancing Content-Based Video-Music Matching using Attention Mechanisms
abstract: In digital storytelling and multimedia production, background music plays a crucial role in shaping the emotional and perceptual experience of viewers. However, selecting appropriate music for video content remains a manual and often subjective process, lacking scalability and contextual sensitivity. To address this, we propose a content-based video music retrieval system that automatically recommends background music based solely on visual input. Our approach leverages deep learning models to extract high-level semantic features from both video and music, enabling perceptually aligned matches without relying on metadata or user input. Specifically, EfficientNet-B5 is used for visual feature extraction, and attention mechanisms are incorporated to enhance the model's focus on emotionally and semantically rich regions of the video. These enriched representations are matched with audio embeddings derived from a VGGish network using cosine similarity in a shared latent space. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed system significantly improves retrieval performance, offering a scalable solution for intelligent music recommendation in video editing and media production.
keywords: Attention Mechanisms | Multimodal Deep Learning | Video Music Retrieval

title: Inspecting Deep Learning Techniques for Music Transcription
abstract: Music Transcription describes the procedure of transforming audio recordings into symbolic formats such as musical notation or scores. This survey explores key methodologies and architectures of symbolic representations, with a focus on feature extraction and deep learning techniques. It begins with rhythm-based and jSymbolic features, followed by advanced frameworks like PiRhDy, MusicBERT, MIDI2vec, and MusicAOG that enhance symbolic music understanding. A comparative analysis of CNN, DNN, and GNN highlights their respective performance and strengths, while RNN are recognized for capturing temporal dependencies and hierarchical structures. Transformer-based models are discussed in terms of optimization strategies, and diffusion techniques are analyzed. Hybrid models that integrate multiple architectures are also reviewed. Core transcription tasks pitch detection, onset/offset estimation, and polyphonic transcription are emphasized for their foundational role. Lastly, the survey covers key datasets and tools essential for benchmarking and advancing symbolic transcription. The observations herein are intended for a wide audience of researchers, engineers, musicians, educators, and music technology developers among others.
keywords: CNN | Diffusion | DNN | Features | GNN | RNN | Transformer

title: A Comprehensive Survey on Machine and Deep Learning Techniques for Genre Prediction in Folk Songs
abstract: Music genre prediction, particularly for folk songs, has become an important area in Music Information Retrieval (MIR), combining computational methods with cultural preservation. This paper evaluates Machine Learning and Deep Learning techniques applied to folk song classification, showcasing progress and remaining gaps. Traditional models such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), Narve Bayes, and Decision Trees are still used but result in limited scalability and cannot capture complex audio patterns. In contrast, modern architectures, including Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional LSTM (Bi-LSTM), and Transformers, deliver stronger performance in genre identification. Analysis of over thirty publications suggests transformer-based models like BERT, DistilBERT, Wav2Vec2, and Audio Spectrogram Transformers (AST) achieve higher accuracy in music genre classification. However, dataset imbalance and underrepresentation of folk music remain challenges. The review concludes by analyzing contributions, datasets, techniques, and limitations across studies, recommending future work focus on multimodal feature integration, transfer learning, and solutions for low-resource folk music domains to ensure improved performance and cultural inclusivity.
keywords: Deep Learning | Folk Songs | Machine Learning | Music Genre Classification | Music Information Re...

title: Novel and Efficient Information-Theoretic Weighted CAT Boost Framework for Complex Multi-Scale Stock Price Prediction
abstract: In this research the long-standing problem of stock price prediction and propose a information gain weighted CatBoost (IGW-CatBoost) approach which orchestrates dynamic feature weighting and sophisticated ensemble learning. In contrast to many traditional and deep learning models which can either consider all TA indicators equally or cannot interpret its learned weights, the method uses information gain to allocate adaptive data driven weights to engineered features to best contribute to the prediction accuracy. These weights are fine-tuned using a gradient-based optimization and then used within a robust CatBoost regression framework. Empirical evaluation of popular NASDAQ stocks (AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, GOOG, TSLA) on daily, hourly, and monthly intervals shows the superiority of IGW-CatBoost in comparison to the state-of-the-art models like CNN-LSTM Hybrid, TFT and N-BEATS (up to 4% higher (R2) (R)R2 and 20% lower error rates). This evidence endorses the predictive effectiveness of dynamic feature weighing and enhances the interpretability and generalization of financial forecasting systems. These results are a significant step toward real-world application, from both a methodological perspective and in terms of practical risk management and algorithmic trading.
keywords: CatBoost | feature weighting | information gain | Stock market prediction

title: Enhancing Store Sales Forecasting Accuracy with Hybrid Deep Learning and LSSVM-Based Models
abstract: Precise sales forecasting is essential for retail enterprises to facilitate effective inventory management, reduce losses, and enhance customer happiness. Conventional statistical models and independent deep learning methods fail to adequately represent the intricate temporal patterns and deviations present in retail sales data. This study introduces a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates neural networks using convolution (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and a Least Squares Support Vector Machine (LSSVM) regressor to enhance forecasting precision. The CNN-LSTM layers extract profound temporal and spatial patterns, but the LSSVM component improves generalisation and rectifies nonlinear residuals. The model was assessed utilising real-world datasets obtained from Kaggle, specifically the Rossman Store Sales and M5 Forecasting datasets. Experimental findings indicate the model's superiority compared to baseline methods like ARIMA, XGBoost, Prophet, and LSTM-only models. The proposed model attained an RMSE of 204.35, MAE of 156.21, MAPE of 3.98%, and a R<sup>2</sup> score of 0.981, surpassing all comparing baselines. These findings confirm the hybrid system's resilience and scalability for real-time retail forecasting applications. The research introduces an innovative and practical forecasting instrument to the domain of intelligent retail analytics.
keywords: ARIMA | Business Intelligence | CNN-LSTM | Demand Forecasting | Ensemble Learning | Feature Engin...

title: Advanced Harmonic Feature Utilization in Ensemble Learning for Guitar Chord Classification
abstract: Guitar chord classification problem has been explored and experimented in more than one dimension for music recognition, classification and recommendation models. Musical notes created by different instruments are just sound waves but harmonised. Mathematically, these sound waves can be represented in both time domain and frequency domain. This mathematical representation becomes necessary for the purpose of analysis and developing recommendation systems for music. Frequency domain representation leads to generation of harmonics which are basically different frequency components contained in an audio specifically music file in our research. The objective of this research paper is to present an optimised ensemble learning on different harmonics generated by guitar playing and subsequently classifying the chord as major or minor guitar chord. Having said that, selection of harmonics is one crucial aspect of this research, where we have also explored the harmonics which are relevant and the ones which are not relevant and can conveniently be dropped. This also helps in dimensionality reduction and controlled computation and time complexity involved in the process of guitar chore classification task. The preprocessing of guitar chords audio into numerical data is computationally extensive. During the preprocessing stage the harmonics are generated in large numbers and the effect of higher order harmonics is explored in some previous works. In this paper we have attempted to implement ensemble machine learning algorithm with tuned hyper parameters. To achieve this we have considered two classification algorithms vis-a-vis Decision Tree and Random Forest algorithms.
keywords: ensemble learning | harmonics | machine learning | music recognition | music recommendation system

title: Decentralized Optical Music Recognition Using YOLO and FedGP for Music Education
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving paradigm for collaborative model training, where data remain on local devices. Leveraging this capability, we explore privacy-aware Optical Music Recognition (OMR) by coupling a state-of-the-art YOLOv9c detector with FedGP, a genetic-programming-based aggregation strategy tailored to highly non-IID client distributions. We cast OMR as the end-to-end transcription of printed and handwritten four-part harmony scores into structured MusicXML, a task complicated by symbol variability, staff-line distortions, and non-musical artifacts. To support this formulation, we assembled a hybrid corpus of 1 810 page images - 810 augmented handwritten exercises and 1000 automati-cally annotated digital scores-comprising 112024 bounding-box annotations across 166 symbol classes. The pages are deliberately partitioned in a non-IID manner among ten virtual clients. Training proceeds by freezing the first 22 layers of the pre-trained YOLOv9c backbone and fine-tuning the detection head for 160 local epochs per client. Parameter updates are transmitted every 20 communication rounds and aggregated over 500 global epochs. Comprehensive experiments show that FedGP consistently outperforms the canonical FedAvg baseline. At communication round 8, FedGP attains a mean mAP50 of 0.6775±0.0179, significantly exceeding FedAvg's 0.6467±0.0095. These findings demonstrate that genetic-programming-driven aggregation mitigates client heterogeneity while preserving data locality and imposing modest computational demands on edge devices. Overall, the study confirms the viability of FL for large-scale, privacy-conscious OMR and establishes FedGP as a robust alternative to standard aggregation schemes under challenging non-IID conditions.
keywords: 4-part harmonization | FedAVG | Federated Learning | FedGP | Optical Music Recognition | YOLOv9

title: A Falsetto Detection Algorithm for Enhancing Voice Gender Recognition
abstract: This paper presents a novel falsetto detection algorithm designed to enhance the performance of Voice Gender Recognition (VGR). By incorporating Signal Processing techniques with insights from vocal pedagogy, our algorithm identifies falsetto in singing voice data to reduce gender identity ambiguity in vocal analysis. We used a pre-trained Deep Learning VGR model to assess the effectiveness of our algorithm. Experiments with various parameter settings demonstrate that the proposed algorithm reduced false positives in male voice detection and improved the VGR F1 score by a maximum of 5.3% for male voices and 2.6% for female voices. Our findings also highlight potential advancements in falsetto detection and provide insight for improving applications such as Voice Age Detection.
keywords: falsetto | falsetto detection | signal processing | singing voice analysis | voice gender recogni...

title: Comparative Analysis of SVM and Random Forest for Smart Grid Stability and Reliability Prediction
abstract: The escalating complexity of smart grid systems, propelled by variable energy demands and heightened incorporation of renewable sources, has intensified the want for precise and prompt stability forecasting. This paper performs a comparative examination of two prevalent machine learning (ML) algorithms Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest (RF) to forecast the stability of smart grids. The research utilizes the Smart Grid Stability and Reliability Dataset from Kaggle, comprising 1000 samples with 24 numerical features that denote key physical and operational elements of the grid. The preprocessing stages encompassed normalization and stratified dataset split to provide balanced training and evaluation. Both models were designed to categorize the grid condition as either stable or unstable. Results indicate that RF achieved a superior prediction accuracy of 98.66%, improving SVM, which reached an accuracy of 94.33%. The exceptional performance of RF is ascribed to its ensemble architecture and capacity to adeptly describe complex nonlinear interactions. This investigation highlights the efficacy of RF as a dependable ML instrument for predicting smart grid reliability. Its exceptional precision renders it ideal for implementation in real-time decision support systems designed to uphold grid reliability and avert system failures.
keywords: Classification | Grid Forecasting | Power Systems | Random Forest (RF) | Reliability Assessment |...

title: Leveraging Ensemble Methods for Accurate Credit Card Fraud Detection
abstract: Credit card fraud presents a risk to financial institutions and individuals, resulting in substantial monetary losses and critical security concerns. Detecting fraudulent transactions in real-time is challenging due to the prevalence of valid transactions and the infrequency of fraud within the entire dataset. Moreover, offenders continually alter their methods. This work established the feasibility of developing an ensemble system utilizing machine learning algorithms, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, and Boost, integrated with the soft voting classifier for the detection of credit card fraud. The algorithms were utilized on both authentic transaction data and generated data to assess their performance according to several metrics, including precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. The experimental results indicated that the ensemble-enhanced outcomes are relatively higher than singular algorithm predictions, reducing false positives while augmenting real positives. This technology is a reliable and adaptable instrument designed to identify probable fraud situations for banks and financial organizations, safeguarding their clients' assets.
keywords: K-means clustering and Decision Tree | Machine learning techniques

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Models and Optimization Techniques for Financial Fraud Detection
abstract: Every day machine learning in financial systems is increasing with financial institutions taking every steps in their power to detect and block counterfeit transactions. Today, modern electronic payment instruments and financial facilities are becoming more and more susceptible to new methods of fraud which are unobtrusively reproducing the activities of legitimate interests to the detriment of the economy which is losing incalculable sums of money. In order to overcome this the combination technique of quantum and classical methods of calculating the data is a great way to enhance the reliability and accuracy of the fraud detection. It is applied by means of Quantum Support Vector Machine, Variational Quantum Classifier, the classical algorithms of Support Vector Machine and K-Nearest Neighbor with an ensemble based on Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization. These algorithms are used together to scan a stream of transactions in real time and classify what is legitimate behaviour and what is unfavourable behaviour. The work provides evidence to prove that hybrid quantum-classical techniques can improve on the performance of classical systems using improved recall, less false negatives and the speed of detection of new types of frauds. It is shown that the integration of quantum intelligence based upon classical methods of analysis is a powerful and fruitful means to enhance levels of secure financial practice and help combat large scale financial frauds in modern digital environments.
keywords: K-Nearest Neighbor | Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization | Quantum Support Vector Machine...

title: Designing Musical Instrument Identification Systems Using Lightweight Machine Learning Architectures
abstract: Musicology is a vast field in which the use of electronic instruments has increased significantly with the development of digital audio workstations and virtual instruments. Selecting the appropriate instrument is crucial for producing high-quality music. The traditional approach to identifying musical instruments relies on manually listening to audio recordings, which is time-consuming and inefficient. Therefore, musical signal processing has become one of the most important tasks in audio signal processing. It enables the identification of instruments in music based on their acoustic features. The proposed work focuses on extracting audio features from WAV files and developing an ensemble model that combines Random Forest and Support Vector Machine classifiers using a voting strategy to identify the instruments used in music. The findings highlight the potential applications of this research in music information retrieval systems and contribute to the growing field of computational musicology by providing a scalable and accurate approach to musical instrument identification, achieving an accuracy of 95%.

title: Hybrid AI-Physics Framework for Lost Circulation Zone Diagnosis: A Data-Driven Iterative Approach Integrating Drilling-Logging Big Data with Theoretical Models
abstract: This paper develops a hybrid AI-physics framework designed to enable real-time, cost-effective diagnosis of loss zones in complex formations. The framework integrates drilling and surface logging big data with physics-based models to address two critical industry challenges: (1) the high uncertainty of manual theoretical calculations and (2) the delays and costs of post-event instrument-based measurements. By using real-time data, it rapidly determines loss zone characteristics (depth, channel type, and fracture dimensions), enhancing treatment success rates and holding the potential to reduce operational costs. A Sichuan Basin database was constructed from over 100 wells using an event-based approach, capturing time-series data around lost circulation events. Theoretical models for determining loss zone depth, identifying lost circulation channel types, and estimating fracture width were evaluated through statistical error analysis. AI optimization methods tailored to each theoretical model were selected, and corresponding AI-physics hybrid models were developed independently, followed by training and validating these models on a database randomly split with 80% allocated for training and 20% for validation. These hybrid models were embedded into the Engineering Intelligent Support Center (EISC) with real-time drilling and surface logging parameters to establish loss zone diagnostic framework. A machine learning-enhanced drilling hydraulics model was developed to calculate the loss zone depth using real-time drilling and surface logging parameters, achieving a test set mean error of 4.06%-4.87%, representing a 10%-48% reduction compared to theoretical models. A convolutional neural network-based intelligent classification model was established to identify lost circulation channel types, leveraging geometric features of loss rate vs. time and mud pit volume vs. time curves to distinguish natural fractures, induced fractures, microfractures/high-permeability pores, and medium-to-large fractures/caverns, with a test set accuracy exceeding 94%. An ensemble learning model integrating AdaBoost with solid- and liquid-phase lost circulation dynamics was constructed to invert fracture width, utilizing drilling fluid or lost circulation material slurry flow data, reducing test set mean errors to 12.07%-42.73%, an improvement of up to 73.46% over theoretical methods. Field trials across over 20 wells in the Sichuan Basin demonstrated that, following post-lost circulation events, engineers could access real-time drilling and surface logging data via the field-deployed Framework connected to the EISC, rapidly determining the loss zone depth, channel type, and fracture width to inform lost circulation control strategies. The framework achieved a field-validated diagnostic accuracy exceeding 85%, with ongoing updates to lost circulation data expected to further enhance precision. This work introduces the first EISC-integrated hybrid AI-physics framework for loss zone diagnosis. It bridges the gap between data-driven AI and physics-based models, enabling rapid, cost-effective diagnosis with acceptable accuracy and without additional downhole instrumentation. The framework offers engineers a practically validated tool for decision-making in lost circulation treatment, balancing theoretical rigor with AI adaptability.

title: Explainable Hate Speech Detection from Audio using Deep Learning
abstract: Majority of the current research studies focused on detecting hate speech require improvements. This is because most studies used textual datasets in English language to train traditional classifiers which are opaque and black-box in nature. This research study proposes a novel and explainable hate speech detection framework from audio for Kiswahili and English languages to curb the above limitations. We utilize a hybrid, complex and robust deep learning architectures consisting of the attention-based LSTM (AT-LSTM) classifier and AT-LSTM-GCNN (Graph CNN) ensemble classifier. An audio hate speech dataset for both languages was manually created by collecting videos from YouTube. After converting the videos to audio, various audio features were extracted to train the deep learning classifiers. Experimental results demonstrate that the AT-LSTM-GCNN ensemble classifier achieved exceptional results in both languages compared to the standalone AT-LSTM. Furthermore, we integrate the attention mechanism and the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) explainability techniques to provide a more granular yet detailed explanation of the predictions achieved by the AT-LSTM classifier.
