title: EEG Channel Selection via h-index-Based Centrality Measures of Complex Networks for Music Genre Classification
abstract: The intrinsic characteristics of music affect the brain by activating specific areas that alter its electrical activity. Understanding this behavior can support relevant applications, but high dimensionality hinders model interpretability, performance, and generalization. Therefore, selecting the most informative channels would reduce complexity, lower computational cost, and potentially improve classification performance. In this paper, we propose an approach to identify the musical genre associated with an acoustic stimulus based on the analysis of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals, aiming to overcome the high dimensionality of the data. To this end, we computed the functional connectivity (graph G) between EEG channels using techniques from various analysis domains, and mined the most representative channels (nodes i). To achieve dimensionality optimization, we propose two centrality measures based on the h-index and degree-strength centrality (DSC) metrics: (1) global ks-index (h<inf>ks</inf>), and (2) local l<inf>ks</inf>-index (l<inf>ks</inf>). High values of h<inf>ks</inf>(G) helped to select the most representative networks, while the computation of l<inf>ks</inf>(i) enabled the identification of the most relevant channels. The selected networks and channels were then mined: the former using global topological measures, and the latter using conventional time-series metrics. In the experiments, we varied the number of the most relevant networks and channels, as well as the DSC type, and used five classifiers with repeated k-fold cross-validation. Our best classification accuracy was 60.1%, achieved with one graph, two channels, and an artificial neural network. The results showed that the new indices helped distinguish subtle structural variations between nodes, select the most relevant channels, and surpass the state of the art in the accuracy–channel ratio.
keywords: Electroencephalography | Graph theory | Machine Learning | Topological measures

title: Comparative Study of Complex Network Centrality Measures for EEG Channel Selection in Music Genre Classification
abstract: Music is a complex auditory stimulus capable of evoking distinct neural responses, measurable through electroencephalographic (EEG) signals. However, its high dimensionality compromises both computational performance and the generalizability of classification models. Therefore, appropriate channel selection becomes essential to improve performance. This study analyzes the use of centrality measures from complex brain connectivity networks for selecting relevant channels in music genre classification. For such a purpose, we constructed Functional Connectivity (FC) networks using correlation, Phase-Locking Value (PLV), and Granger Causality (GC), and evaluated various centrality measures. In addition to conventional centralities, we considered a degree-strength-based metric, which also served as the basis for the development of a new one, named Bonacich Degree-Strength (BDS), with three variants. The feature vector was composed of attributes extracted from the most central channel, combined with topological metrics. Using repeated Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) resampling (10 iterations) and various classifiers, we conducted several experiments with each FC method and each centrality measure. The results showed that with an artificial neural network, GC, and only one channel, the channel selection guided by the betweenness centrality measure improved classification performance in most FC types and classifiers, achieving a maximum accuracy of 60.4%. Furthermore, the BDS variant based on a basal vector and a degree-strength adjacency matrix exhibited discriminative power comparable to the corresponding conventional measure. Additionally, our best model outperformed most state-of-the-art models in terms of the trade-off between accuracy, number of channels, and total number of features. These findings reinforce the role of complex networks as a robust tool in the analysis of neurophysiological signals.
keywords: Biological Signal Classification | Centrality Measures | Complex Networks | Machine Learning

title: Hybrid Machine Learning Algorithms for Solving the Multi-class Classification Problem of Liver Damage Stages
abstract: This comprehensive methodology leveraging hybrid machine learning is proposed for the processing of incomplete medical datasets and the prediction of concurrent liver fibrosis (F1-F4) and steatosis (S1-S4). The core of our contribution is a three-stage system combining hybrid imputation (KNN+MICE), PLS-neural network-based factor analysis for identifying significant biomarkers (ALT, AST, bilirubin), and an optimized Voting classifier ensemble (SVM, RF, k-NN) with automatic weight tuning, yielding an F1-score of 0.96. Experimental validation on 104 patient records confirmed a statistically significant performance advantage over isolated methods, with a 15.9% increase in accuracy (p<0.05). The practical relevance of this research is embodied in a high-precision diagnostic instrument with an interactive web interface, designed for seamless clinical deployment and forming a foundation for unified clinical decision support systems in hepatology.
keywords: classification | data imputation | ensemble learning | hybrid machine learning methods | incomple...

title: A SHAP-Based Explainable AI Approach for Dropout Prediction Using Ensemble Stacking Models
abstract: Student dropout is a critical issue in higher education, affecting both academic achievement and institutional performance. Many existing predictive models lack the required accuracy and interpretability for timely interventions. This study proposes a stacking ensemble model integrated with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to increase the transparency of the model and prediction accuracy. The ensemble includes Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forests (RF), and LightGBM as base learners, with Logistic Regression (LR) acting as the meta-learner. The dataset was partitioned using stratified sampling to ensure a balanced class distribution between testing and training subsets. The proposed model achieved excellent performance, with an accuracy of 98.34%, precision of 99.32%, recall of 96.61%, F1-score of 97.95%, and AU-ROC of 99.92%. SHAP analysis identified critical predictors like the quantity of approved curricular units, tuition payment status, and scholarship eligibility as highly influential in estimating the risk of dropout. The incorporation of SHAP enabled interpretability on a local and global level, providing valuable perspectives on how the model comes to its conclusions. In conclusion, the proposed framework delivers high predictive performance along with interpretable outputs, making it a useful instrument for early warning systems in higher education.
keywords: Explainable AI | Model Interpretability | SHAP | Stacking Ensemble | Student Dropout

title: A Novel Voice-Processing Method Leveraging Polyphonic Audio for Instrument Recognition Using Machine Learning
abstract: In this research, a novel polyphonic voice recognition system for instrument identification, pitch detection, and chord detection based on machine learning techniques is presented. The system utilizes python and its large set of data analytics libraries to provide efficient and realistic audio recognition. Some of the main techniques involve Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) for feature extraction and classification models like k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) and hidden Markov models (hmm). MFCC s have been used to efficiently extract the spectral features of the audio signals, whereas K-NN classifiers (k=3) and hmm models (8 gaussian states) yield high instrument identification and sequential pattern audio analysis. The system also presents high accuracies of 58% using K-NN and 67% using hmm in classifying 8 instruments namely acoustic guitar, bass drum, cello, clarinet, double bass, flute, hi hat, saxophone, snare drum, violin. A stratified shuffle split strategy and a balanced dataset guarantee fair training and testing. The frontend, coded in html, CSS, and JavaScript, supports dynamic audio visualization and easy user interaction through web audio Api, whereas the backend, implemented with python and flask, processes real-time audio and machine learning operations. Iterative feedback-based updates enhance system flexibility even further, which makes it worthwhile for use in music education, production, transcription, and research applications. In spite of difficulties in overlapping sound separation and intricate polyphonic audio analysis, this research emphasizes the revolutionary potential of intelligent audio processing in developing music technology.
keywords: audio signal processing | bass drum | cello | clarinet | double bass | flute | hi hat | hmm | K-N...

title: Towards Explainable Music Emotion Recognition for Guitar Improvisations
abstract: Explainability has gained significant attention across various domains, yet it remains relatively underexplored in the field of music, particularly in Music Emotion Recognition. This paper presents XMERApp; a web application designed to provide interpretability for a deep learning model that classifies classical and acoustic guitar into four emotional states. Our system employs a deep learning architecture trained on improvised musical performances to classify emotions, while providing comprehensive explainability through multiple complementary approaches. The application offers users three levels of interpretability: (1) detailed breakdowns of prediction probabilities across different emotion categories, enabling users to understand the confidence and uncertainty in model predictions; (2) temporal visualization of emotion evolution throughout the improvisation, revealing how the model's understanding of emotional content develops over time; and (3) LIME-based explanations that highlight specific spectrogram regions most influential to the model's decisions within focused time windows. Additionally, users can listen to the specific spectrogram regions identified as critical for the emotion classification, gaining insights into which parts of the performance and frequency ranges contributed the most to the model's output. The web-based nature of XMERApp enables deployment across many devices, including smart musical instruments, enhancing the interpretability of intelligent features embedded within them.
keywords: Emotion Recognition | Explainable Artificial Intelligence | Music Information Retrieval

title: Automatic Music Generation Using LSTM and Transformers
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence has provided new opportunities for natural music creation through automatic music generation the subsequent creation of complex composing music therefore requires a lesser engagement of the user. This work describes a new framework for creating music based on deep learning methods, including LSTM and Transformer models. The system extends Sequence Analysis to MIDI sequences, utilizes LSTM models to learn temporal dependencies, and generates new music using Encoder-Decoder Transformers in the sequence-to-sequence framework to enhance the output into contextually structured musical developments. The presented approach also has additional advantages because it completely eliminates the particular domain's architecture of the models and relies on more general sequence-to-sequence models, which makes the pipeline less complicated and thus more scalable. The end product is the production of MIDI sequences, which, with the aid of synthesizers, are transformed into audio that appears to be original and of superior quality. This work shows the possibility of synthesizing LSTM and Transformer models in music generation and solves such issues as data heterogeneity, low-performance computations, and easy understanding of generated melody. The presented framework opens the path toward improvements in music information retrieval approaches and AI music generation.
keywords: Audio Synthesis | Automatic Music Generation | Deep Learning | LSTM | MIDI Processing | Music Inf...

title: Classification of Song Genre Based on Textual Lyrics and Song Profile Information
abstract: This study proposes a machine learning-based approach for the classification of song genre using textual lyrics and song profile information. Song genre classification is an important task in the field of music information retrieval, as it enables music industry professionals to analyze and understand music trends and to make informed decisions about music production and marketing. This paper will perform pre-processing of lyrical data from songs and perform machine learning tasks to classify the genre by using machine learning algorithms such as Support Vector Machine, Recurrent Neural Networks and Attention architecture. To enhance the outcomes, hyperparameter tuning will be performed. Finally, the output from each model is compared by using suitable performance assessment measures and the best machine learning algorithm to classify song genre can be obtained.
keywords: Classification | Machine Learning | Natural Language Processing | Song genre | Text

title: Dual-Feature Ensemble Deep Learning Architecture for Robust Spoofing Speech Detection
abstract: In this paper, we propose a spoofing speech detection method using a deep learning model based on a dual-feature ensemble. The threat of spoofing speech attacks has increased with the advancements in speech synthesis and voice conversion technologies. This highlights the need for highly accurate spoofing speech detection methods. Our proposed method leverages information extracted from waveforms and mel spectrograms to enhance the robustness of spoofing speech detection. By combining a state-of-the-art spoofing detection technique with a high-performing model from sound-related tasks, we aim to develop a robust system for spoofing speech detection. Evaluation experiments using the ASVspoof 2021 dataset show that the proposed model outperforms conventional methods, including the wav2vec2.0 + AASIST baseline. Our experimental results suggest that the proposed method captures various characteristics of speech from multiple angles, thereby improving the generalization performance of the model.
keywords: Deep learning | Feature ensemble | Spoofing speech detection

title: LLM-Based Dysarthric Communication Aid with Text and Voice Output
abstract: Speech recognition technology still does not meet the needs of a majority of people who suffer from dysarthria. Existing systems provide transcripts that end up being broken and disjointed and grammatically flawed and unable to convey speaker intended meaning. Such systems regard transcription as the end of the conversation process rather than the beginning points for understanding. This paper comes up with a new assistive system that employs post-processing to build meaning in an intelligent way. The system's core works on FLAN-T5-Large that acts as a robust language model to reason about contextual information and semantic relations. The system works through three interdependent steps: the initial step utilizes a Whisper ASR model specifically trained on dysarthric speech to translate audio into raw text. The language model then applies this text to create meaningful fluent language that mirrors what the speaker wished to say. The last part of the system employs a Text-to-Speech synthesizer to transcribe the corrected text into natural and expressive speech output. The system converts disfluent input into comprehensible expression to enable people with dysarthria to communicate fluently.
keywords: Accessibility | AI-driven communication aid | Assistive technology | Automatic Speech Recognition...

title: Music Genre Classification Using Multilayer Perceptron: A Machine Learning Approach
abstract: Music genre classification is an important task in digital library organization, and is beneficial to recommender systems. In this work, we explore the possible use of a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) to solve genre classification tasks using audio features as input, such as MFCCs, chroma features, and spectral contrast, among others, and signal processing approaches such as STFT, Mel spectrograms, and spectral rolloff. The proposed model also outperformed the traditional classifiers such as KNN, SVM, and Random Forest when tested on the GTZAN dataset with a test accuracy of 92.19% and a validation accuracy of 92.22%. Experiments demonstrate that the lightweight neural models, such as MLP, can achieve comparable performance with deeper CNN/RNN architectures and have computational advantages in scenarios of real-world applications, e.g., automated genre tagging, personalized recommendations, and content curation in music streaming platforms.
keywords: Audio Feature | Chroma Features | GTZAN Dataset | Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) | Music Genre Class...

title: Audio Data Analysis and Music Genre Classification with Various Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Music genre classification presents several challenges, including high-dimensional audio data, overlapping genre characteristics, and subjective labeling. Although machine learning has shown promise in addressing these challenges, many studies either focus on a narrow range of models or lack comparative performance insights. In this study, we perform a comprehensive evaluation of ten machine learning algorithms for music genre classification using the widely adopted GTZAN dataset. The models include Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machines, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest, Neural Networks, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), among others. Our results demonstrate that XGBoost achieved the highest accuracy at 90.09%, outperforming Random Forest (81.42%) and KNN (80.58%) by a significant margin. Feature importance analysis highlights that percussive, harmonic, and spectral features contribute most substantially to genre discrimination. Notably, XGBoost's superior performance suggests its ability to effectively capture non-linear patterns in musical features, offering a strong alternative to traditional classifiers. This work contributes a broad comparative analysis and emphasizes the effectiveness of ensemble-based approaches in music genre classification, providing valuable insights for future research and practical applications in music information retrieval.
keywords: Feature Importance | GTZAN Dataset | Machine Learning | Music Genre Classification | Signal Proce...

title: Thermal imaging-based fault detection and energy efficiency analysis in a 1.6 MW photovoltaic system in Bağyurdu OIZ, Türkiye
abstract: The present study assesses the influence of thermal imaging defect detection on the energy efficiency of a 1.6 MW solar power facility in the Bağyurdu Organized Industrial Zone (OIZ) in İzmir, Turkey. Thermal imaging has demonstrated efficacy in detecting serious problems in photovoltaic (PV) panels, including hot spots, inoperative modules, faulty connections, and shadowing, which substantially impact system performance. A comprehensive investigation revealed that around 15% of the photovoltaic panels displayed defects, resulting in a 16% decrease in system performance and an estimated yearly energy loss of 0.35 GWh. The study emphasizes the benefits of thermal imaging compared to conventional fault detection techniques, including its capacity for swift and non-invasive identification of localized overheating, which may lead to fires, and its ability to discern fluctuations in energy output due to shading or malfunctioning modules. The results underscore the necessity for routine thermal evaluations and maintenance to guarantee photovoltaic systems’ operational efficacy and dependability. This study enhances the sparse data on large-scale photovoltaic systems in Türkiye and illustrates the effectiveness of thermal imaging as an economical and accurate diagnostic instrument. Future studies should amalgamate thermal imaging with sophisticated diagnostic techniques, like electroluminescence testing and machine learning, to augment fault detection precision and optimize photovoltaic system efficacy.
keywords: dc/ac ratio optimization | energy efficiency | fault detection | photovoltaic systems | solar ene...

title: Accuracy Improvement of Automatic Chord Recognition with Source Separation Preprocessing
abstract: Automatic chord recognition is a fundamental research topic in music information retrieval (MIR) and has been applied to various tasks, including cover song retrieval and music key detection. In recent years, several methods based on deep learning have been proposed, enabling easier and more accurate recognition. In this study, we focused on the bi-directional Transformer for musical chord recognition (BTC), a chord recognition method based on Transformers, and evaluated its performance. The experimental results showed that the chord recognition accuracy for the triads was 75.52%, which is insufficient for realworld music applications. To improve the recognition accuracy, we focus on the differences in volume between instruments within a song. We propose a method that emphasizes sounds from chord-relevant instruments by applying source separation as a preprocessing step. By amplifying the volume of pitched instruments, such as a piano and guitar, we confirmed that the proposed method successfully corrected more than 2,000 misrecognized chord frames and improved the overall recognition accuracy compared with the conventional method.

title: An Ensemble Framework for an Effective Feature Extraction and Classification of Chinese Ethnic Music Styles
abstract: China's vast and ancient cultural landscape encompasses 56 ethnic groups with distinct musical traditions, presenting significant challenges for automated Feature Extraction and classification due to subtle tonal variations, diverse instrumental timbres, and limited digitized archives. With the usage of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) algorithms, classification performance still can be enhanced for an efficient Feature Extraction. However, these models suffers from poor feature extraction methods to understand the complex Chinese music tones. To solve this above problem, this research presents a comprehensive framework for intelligent classification of Chinese ethnic music styles using Mel-Frequency cepstral Co-efficient(MFCC) extraction, and Optimized Kolomorgy Arnold training networks. The suggested model are used for classification of Chinese Music variants The comprehensive training was carried out using the Kaggle Chinese Ethnic Music datasets and validated using enactment boundaries such as accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, F1-score are measured and evaluated. The extensive evaluation is carried out and performance of the proposed framework demonstrated its superiority over the other existing frameworks, achieving the accuracy rate of 98.56%, precision of 98.3%, recall of 98.2% and F1-scoreof 98.4% in Feature Extraction and classifying the different Chinese music styles.

title: Segment Transformer: AI-Generated Music Detection via Music Structural Analysis
abstract: Audio and music generation systems have been remarkably developed in the music information retrieval (MIR) research field. The advancement of these technologies raises copyright concerns, as ownership and authorship of AI-generated music (AIGM) remain unclear. Also, it can be difficult to determine whether a piece was generated by AI or composed by humans clearly. To address these challenges, we aim to improve the accuracy of AIGM detection by analyzing the structural patterns of music segments. Specifically, to extract musical features from short audio clips, we integrated various pre-trained models, including self-supervised learning (SSL) models or an audio effect encoder, each within our suggested transformerbased framework. Furthermore, for long audio, we developed a segment transformer that divides music into segments and learns inter-segment relationships. We used the FakeMusicCaps and SONICS datasets, achieving high accuracy in both the short-audio and full-audio detection experiments. These findings suggest that integrating segment-level musical features into long-range temporal analysis can effectively enhance both the performance and robustness of AIGM detection systems.

title: The Application of Computer Software and Hybrid Learning Framework in Chemical and Chemical Engineering Data Processing
abstract: Chemical Engineering and Chemical analyses poses a significant challenges due to device-specific variations, inconsistent peak identification, specification of spectral noises across the different instruments, which limiting the crossplatform and analytical reliability. Hence application of computer software in chemical and chemical engineering data processing has become vital for enhancing efficiency, accuracy, and predictive capabilities in modern industries. The proposed model incorporates spatial embeddings, temporal decomposition, and an attention-based feature fusion strategy with a region-aware hybrid random forest ensemble. To boost the quality of inputs, dimensionality reduction is achieved by Relief), whereas Wavelet Transform eliminates economic time series noise. The structure of the model is fine-tuned with Bayesian hyperparameter tuning for enhanced generalization. Experiments have been performed on Kaggle's Raman Spectroscopy devices from the different manfacturers. The suggested model proposed obtained an R<sup>2</sup> value of 0.964 and RMSE of 0.031, which is higher than what conventional models such as ARIMA, SVR, and XGBoost would obtain. The feature importance analysis came up with catalyst efficiency, reaction temperature control, and material purity levels as the most influential drivers. The framework provides chemical engineers and process designers with a strong and interpretable forecasting, early warning, and targeted process optimization tool.

title: A Comparative Study of Statistical Features and Deep Learning for Orchestral Texture Classification
abstract: Orchestral texture, which reflects the interaction of instruments in ensemble music, is central to understanding multitrack music; however, symbolic texture classification has not been widely studied. This study addresses the task of assigning textural roles to individual track-bar units (i.e., each bar of each track) in symphonic movements. We evaluate a range of features and models, including random forest, convolutional neural networks, hybrid approaches, and pre-trained models, on the Orchestration and S3 datasets. The results show that duration-related statistical features are the most informative, while identifying melodic roles remains challenging. Overall, our findings suggest the potential of symbolic texture classification, and highlight key challenges in melody extraction for multi-track music and ensuring labeling consistency across datasets.

title: An Ensemble-based Approach for Accurate Classification of Astronomical Objects using Deep Learning
abstract: With the rapid growth of telescopic technologies and space exploration missions, the amount of astronomical data captured as images, videos, and audio from satellites has increased significantly. Manually classifying such large datasets is no longer practical, making automated solutions necessary. Most existing studies focus on limited binary or three-class classification tasks, which leaves a gap in models that can handle a wider range of celestial objectsIn this paper, we propose a novel five-class ensemble deep learning model for the classification of planets, comets, asteroids, black holes, and constellations. Our method combines the advantages of VGG19, which is renowned for its effective layered feature extraction, with ResNet101V2, which is known for its residual connections and capacity to train deep networks effectively. The ensemble achieves a validation accuracy of 95.7% and a training accuracy of 99.7% using a soft voting technique. These outcomes show how well the model performs in classifying multi-class astronomical images and offer a potent instrument for enhancing automated analysis in space exploration.
keywords: Ensemble Model | Image Classification | ResNet101V2 | Soft Voting | VGG-19

title: Deep Learning based Spectrogram Analysis for Music Genre Classification
abstract: The large prevalence of digital music has created a pressing need for efficient and accurate automatic music genre classification systems. Traditional approaches rely on manual feature extraction, thus limiting scalability and generalizability across diverse genres of music. The project aims to address the problem of ineffective genre classification by using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to learn hierarchical audio features end-to-end from raw audio. The aim is to enhance accuracy, flexibility, and real-time performance of music classification systems. The system converts audio waves into Log-Mel spectrograms, thus extracting temporal and frequency features necessary for genre discrimination. CNNs automatically detect intricate patterns from these visual representations without human intervention with improved performance across a wide range of genres. The novelty is in the combination of spectrogram-based preprocessing with state-of-the-art CNN architectures and performance optimization methods that reduce training time with improved robustness. Experimental outcomes show impressive improvements in accuracy and scalability, thus placing the system on the road towards deployment in today's music platforms.
keywords: Audio Signal Interpretation | Deep Learning | Digital Music | Genre Recognition | Intelligent Sys...

title: Music Genre Classification Using Spectrograms and AlexNet: A Deep Learning Approach with MFCC and Spectral Features
abstract: Music, an art form that blends vocal and instrumental sounds to create beauty, harmony, and emotional depth, significantly influences both the fields of music and dance as well as everyday life. This study explores the classification of 10 music genres using the GTZAN dataset, using Mel frequency spectral coefficients (MFCC) and spectral features, namely centrion, bandwidth, contrast and roll-off, to construct a 450-dimensional feature vector. Deep learning models, specifically VGG16 and AlexNet, along with traditional machine learning classifiers, to assess classification performance.AlexNet outperforms all of them with the highest accuracy of 97.4% even though more common CNNs are trained. The results imply that deep learning models work well on spectrograms for the purpose of genre classification. Nevertheless enables broader datasets method development facilitates dataset bias and limited research generalisability across styles; prompting larger datasets need development. Not only does this research contribute to the state of the art in audio classification, it also addresses a societal and humanitarian concern that aligns with UN SDG 17 of promoting technological advancements and international partnerships to make music accessible to everyone.

title: Deep Transfer Learning for Indian Classical Music Genre Classification
abstract: A transfer learning approach for Indian music genre classification is presented, leveraging a fine-tuned Wav2Vec2 model. The system achieves 88.7% (best performance at epoch 89) accuracy across five genres (Bollypop, Carnatic, Ghazal, Hindustani, Qawwali) on a curated dataset of 115 audio recordings with a final model accuracy of 85%. A comprehensive evaluation is provided, including confusion matrix, per-class accuracy, and classification report and genre-specific challenges and model strengths are discussed. The results highlight the promise of speech-based deep models for culturally rich, underrepresented music traditions.
keywords: Audio Analysis | Classification Report | Confusion Matrix | Deep Learning | Indian Classical Musi...

title: Local Equivariance Error-Based Metrics for Evaluating Sampling-Frequency-Independent Property of Neural Network
abstract: Audio signal processing methods based on deep neural networks (DNNs) are typically trained only at a single sampling frequency (SF) and therefore require signal resampling to handle untrained SFs. However, recent studies have shown that signal resampling can degrade performance with untrained SFs. This problem has been overlooked because most studies evaluate only the performance at trained SFs. In this paper, to assess the robustness of DNNs to SF changes, which we refer to as the SF-independent (SFI) property, we propose three metrics to quantify the SFI property on the basis of local equivariance error (LEE). LEE measures the robustness of DNNs to input transformations. By using signal resampling as input transformation, we extend LEE to measure the robustness of audio source separation methods to signal resampling. The proposed metrics are constructed to quantify the SFI property in specific network components responsible for predicting time-frequency masks. Experiments on music source separation demonstrated a strong correlation between the proposed metrics and performance degradation at untrained SFs.
keywords: audio source separation | deep learning | Local equivariance error | sampling frequency

title: Integrating High Order Ambisonics and Deep Learning for Advanced Instrument Separation in Spatial Audio Applications
abstract: This work explores the integration of Higher-Order Ambisonics (HOA) and deep learning for advanced sound source separation in spatial audio applications. We present a computationally efficient spherical harmonics (SH) beamforming framework that extracts spatial components from raw microphone array recordings. Our methodology leverages SH-based spatial filtering combined with a deep learning de-bleeding model, enhancing source separation in audio applications. We evaluate the performance of the SH beamformer and neural network model both independently and in combination, demonstrating that the proposed pipeline achieves superior source isolation while maintaining high signal fidelity. Unlike previous studies that relied on synthetic data, our approach is validated with real-world recordings captured using a third-order spherical microphone array. Results highlight the effectiveness of integrating spatial domain filtering with deep learning for reducing interference and enhancing separation quality. Furthermore, we provide an open-source implementation of our approach to encourage its adoption in spatial audio processing tasks, including music production. Our findings pave the way for a portable-studio paradigm, relying solely on an HOA array.
keywords: Ambisonics | Deep Learning | Music Production | Real-world Recordings | Source Separation | Spati...

title: EfficientNetV2-ResNet50V2 Ensemble Framework for Parkinson’s Disease Detection: Optimized Class Balancing and Test-Time Augmentation
abstract: Early detection of Parkinson’s Disease (PD) remains a significant c linical c hallenge d espite i ts i mpact o n treatment efficacy a nd p atient o utcomes. T his s tudy p resents a specialized computational framework utilizing dual-network architecture to identify diagnostic biomarkers from functional MRI (fMRI) data. The research addresses critical neuroimaging constraints—the scarcity of annotated samples and pronounced class imbalance—through a purpose-built methodology integrating adaptive data augmentation with an architecture-optimized ensemble approach. By strategically combining the distinct feature extraction strengths of EfficientNetV2 a nd R esNet50V2 n etworks with custom regularization techniques, the system achieves exceptional diagnostic performance: 94.3% accuracy, 93.1% precision, and 95.7% recall on independent validation data. The diagnostic algorithm demonstrates robust discriminative capabilities with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.968, surpassing existing methodologies by 7.2%. These findings s uggest p otential clinical utility as an assistive diagnostic instrument that could facilitate earlier intervention for PD patients.

title: Deepfake Voice Detection: Countering Deepfake Audio with Deep Learning Architectures
abstract: The active development of the Text-to-Speech (TTS) technology as well as the Voice Conversion (VC) has posed an outstanding danger to the digital security. To overcome this obstacle, this paper will compare and contrast systematically three different deep learning structures, a hybrid CNN-RNN framework that aims to conduct both spectral and temporal artifact processing, a CNN-LSTM ensemble framework exploring the distinctive capabilities of the spatial and temporal processing, and a state-of-the-art system with Wav2Vec2 as a pre-trained feature extractor and as a Light Convolutional Neural Network (LCNN) to make predictions. Although all these architectures operate on the basis of known elements, they are new in the way that they specifically aim at deepfake detection and also they are assessed and evaluated in an unprecedented way in parallel. With experiments on a wide variety of benchmark datasets, such as ASVspoof 2019, WaveFake and FoR, this paper compares the trade-offs between feature-engineered and self-supervised methods. As the results show, CNN + LSTM-based platform can deliver better results, its analysis accuracy is 99.81, because it is able to get deep, context-sensitive representations of unprocessed audio. The present study highlights the symbiosis of organizing various deep learning techniques and establishes a complete reference in future studies in resilient equipment of deepfake voice detecting.
keywords: CNN-RNN | Deepfake | Ensemble Learning | Voice Detection | Wav2Vec2

title: Data Augmentation Methods for Music Removal from Environmental Sounds Based on Machine Learning
abstract: With the rapid growth of video-sharing platforms and social networking services in recent years, video posting has become increasingly active. When videos include copyrighted music, it is necessary to remove the music in accordance with copyright regulations. Traditionally, music removal has been performed using speech enhancement and signal processingbased source separation methods. However, speech enhancement tends to unintentionally remove non-Target sounds, while signal processing-based source separation requires selecting the target sound to be removed for each case. To overcome these issues, a deep learning-based music removal method has been proposed that neither eliminates speech audio nor requires manual target selection. Nevertheless, its removal accuracy remains insufficient, likely due to the limited quantity of available training music data. A promising solution is to apply data augmentation to improve performance. Although data augmentation techniques have been developed for other audio domains, no suitable method for music data has been proposed. Therefore, in this study, we propose a data augmentation approach using pitch shifting, evaluating music removal performance for each pitch scale under the twelve-Tone equal temperament, and examining appropriate pitch shifting values and applicable ranges.
keywords: Conv-TasNet | Copyright protection | Data augmentation | Environmental sounds | Machine learning ...

title: Enhancing Music Genre Classification using Ensemble and Deep Learning Approaches
abstract: The proliferation of digital music has generated vast amounts of audio data, necessitating efficient methods for music genre classification. This paper explores the use of machine learning, deep learning, and ensemble approaches to classify music genres based on audio features. From the popular GTZAN dataset, two types of feature datasets are considered, one with original 30-sec and other with segmented 3-sec audio files. Various feature extraction techniques are applied over each audio music files to obtain the mean and variance as feature vectors. We began by examining the performance of different baseline machine learning models, 1-D Convolutional Neural Network(CNN) model followed by various ensemble techniques such as bagging, boosting, stacking and voting. The experimental results indicate that ensemble methods significantly outperform individual models in terms of accuracy, reliability, and generalization. Specifically, voting ensemble model achieves superior performance with an accuracy of 78% and 89% for classifying music genres considering both the original 30-sec and segmented 3-sec datasets.
keywords: Bagging | Boosting | CNN | Music Genre Classification | Stacking | Voting

title: Robust Deepfake Speech Algorithm Recognition: Classifying Generative Algorithms via Speaker X-Vectors and Deep Learning
abstract: The rapid advancement of deepfake voice technologies has resulted in alarming cases of impersonation and deception, highlighting the urgent need for robust tools that can not only distinguish real audio from fake but also recognise the generative algorithms responsible. The ability to not only detect deepfake audio but also recognise the generative methods used is essential for forensic investigations, legal proceedings, and regulatory enforcement. Without robust and explainable detection frameworks, legal professionals and investigators lack the tools needed to effectively monitor, investigate, and prosecute cases involving deepfake misuse. In this work, we take a voice biometrics approach, shifting the focus from identifying who is speaking to identifying which algorithm is speaking. Doing so allows our approach to inherently handle unseen classes while achieving competitive performance for deepfake speech algorithm recognition. Our system leverages a voice-focused ResNet101-based x-vector extraction model and combines diverse audio features, and our experimental novel feature LFCC-HF, enhanced with Linear Discriminant Analysis and cosine similarity clustering. This approach allows for a more transparent and interpretable decision-making process by usinga single voice similarity decision boundary compared to the ensemble-based methods commonly used in the literature. Unlike previous works that rely on an ensemble of models, which convolute the decision-making process, our method achieves comparable results while using a significantly lighter-weight architecture, with our model having 14.84 M parameters compared to 95 M and 317 M parameters for Wav2Vec2 base and large. Furthermore, we demonstrate the benefits of targeted data augmentation, which, combined with feature fusion and our novel feature, improves system robustness and adaptability, increasing our F1 Score from 0.624 to 0.763, a 22.275% increase over our best single feature, and a 40.775% increase over the best ADD 2023 Track 3 baseline. Importantly, the system achieves interpretability through its back-end classification process, where decisions are based on a transparent, learned threshold for voice similarity to known voiceprints. This work offers a foundation for advancing more robust and interpretable solutions in the field of deepfake speech detection.
keywords: Deepfake Audio | Deepfake Detection | Generative Algorithm Recognition | Synthetic Speech Detection

title: BOARD # 320: An AI-Enhanced System to Integrate Unstructured Observations with Formal Engineering Education: An NSF RITEL Project
abstract: This article outlines the objectives, design, recent findings, and anticipated outcomes of a newly funded research initiative supported by the National Science Foundation (NSF). The project is part of the Research on Innovative Technologies for Enhanced Learning (RITEL) program, which prioritizes pioneering research in emerging teaching and learning technologies tailored to address critical challenges in real-world educational contexts. The primary aim of the project is to create, implement, and assess an AI-driven learning platform in the format of a mobile application called CeLens that acts as an on-demand educator to help construction engineering students learn from their unstructured observations during everyday activities. CeLens seamlessly merges students’ observations during everyday experiences or formal site visits with their formal engineering education. The platform, designed based on the activity learning theory and developed based on human-centered principles, leverages advanced hybrid image-audio processing techniques to accurately and efficiently identify and explain diverse construction elements. The envisioned AI-enhanced learning system will be designed based on the Activity Learning Theory, which asserts that the human mind is an integral part of environmental interactions and positions activity, whether sensory, mental, or physical, as a precursor to learning. The AI-enhanced platform will be designed based on human-centered principles and will operate using a novel hybrid image-audio processing system that can efficiently and effectively recognize and classify various construction components. In addition to integrating imagery and audio data through this novel hybrid approach, the project will introduce two major technological innovations in audio processing and sound recognition. First, the hybrid use of collected audio and imagery data will improve the overall performance of the system by capturing a more comprehensive range of construction components and operations. Second, by using innovative audio processing and signal source separation algorithms, the need for multiple microphones will be eliminated, enabling the entire system to be encapsulated in a single device (i.e., a student's smartphone) with the ability to sense and analyze audio signals from distances of up to 100 feet. Throughout this project, the proposed AI-enhanced teaching and learning approach will be implemented in multiple undergraduate construction engineering courses to empirically evaluate its effectiveness on students' learning processes and outcomes, as well as the perceptions of both students and educators regarding this innovation as a formal pedagogical method. Although the AI-enhanced learning platform will be developed in the context of construction engineering, the proposed learning method and the intellectual merit of this project can be transferred to other disciplines. This project will also assess the broader applicability of the proposed innovation.

title: Ensemble Machine Learning-Based Approach to Predict Human Mental States with Optimized Feature Selection and Data Balancing
abstract: The quality of life is greatly impacted by mental health illnesses worldwide, making sophisticated diagnostic instruments that strike a compromise between precision and interpretability necessary. This paper uses the DASS-42 dataset (n = 39,775) to predict stress, anxiety, and depression using a unique machine learning architecture that uses a stacking ensemble of k-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Trees, and Multi-Layer Perceptron. In order to solve class imbalance and guarantee robust feature scaling, the model incorporates Yeo-Johnson transformations, Min-Max normalization, and NRS Boundary-SMOTE for data balancing. Grid Search and Nested Cross-Validation are used to maximize hyperparameter tuning, resulting in 99.94% (depression), 99.92% (anxiety), and 99.92% (stress) accuracy. The framework bridges the gap between predictive capacity and transparency, making it a dependable tool for clinical mental health evaluations due to its high accuracy and interpretability. This method offers a scalable, reliable solution for mental health diagnostics and advances AI-driven psychological treatments, opening the door for early diagnosis and individualized therapy.
keywords: DASS-42 | Data imbalance | Machine learning | Mental health | NRS Boundary-SMOTE | Stacking Ensemble

title: Research on Intelligent Retrieval Technology of Digital Music Database Based on Deep Learning
abstract: Traditional music information retrieval technology relies on keyword matching and metadata filtering, which is difficult to meet the complex and diverse retrieval needs of users. In this paper, an intelligent retrieval technology of digital music database based on deep learning is proposed. By constructing an efficient deep neural network (DNN) model, automatic extraction and intelligent matching of music features are realized. Research methods include multi-dimensional feature extraction of audio signal, DNN architecture design and multi-task learning optimization strategy. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the proposed model in music classification task is 91.8%, and the F1-score is 90.3%, which is significantly better than the traditional method and the deep learning baseline model. In the cross-data set retrieval task, the mAP@10 index of the multitask learning version model is improved by 5-15% among different data sets, showing stronger generalization ability. In addition, the analysis of ablation experiments shows that the introduction of BiLSTM, attention mechanism and multi-task learning all contribute significantly to the performance improvement.
keywords: DEEP LEARNING | DEEP NEURAL NETWORK | DIGITAL MUSIC DATABASE | INTELLIGENT RETRIEVAL TECHNOLOGY

title: Utilising generative AI to assist in the creation and production of Chinese popular music
abstract: Background: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has had a significant impact on the music industry, particularly Chinese popular music (C-pop), which presents unique difficulties due to its distinctive melodic structures and emotional depth. While AI can boost efficiency and inspire composers, current models are ineffective in feature selection and prediction accuracy, leading to compositions without stylistic integrity and commercial viability. Problem Statement: Current AI-generated melodies often lack the stylistic depth of human compositions and fail to predict market success accurately. These challenges highlight the need for a more effective AI framework capable of generating high-quality melodies. Objectives: This study introduces the GenAI Melody-LSTM algorithm. This generative AI-driven technique uses Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to create melodies inspired by Chinese pop songs and forecasts their success. The main goals are to build an AI pipeline for music preprocessing, improve feature selection, train a deep learning model for stylistically consistent melodies, and compare its effectiveness to other methods. Methodology: The methodology utilises a GenAI Melody-LSTM algorithm, which contains data preprocessing techniques such as mode and mean imputation, label encoding, and Min-Max scaling. Feature selection is improved using the Hybrid Filter-Wrapper Ensemble (HFWE) method, which combines Mutual Information, Chi-Square Test, ANOVA F-Test, and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) with Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), with the final subset determined by majority voting. The selected features, like melody structure, key signature, tempo, rhythm complexity, instrumentation, and emotion, are used as inputs for an LSTM-based deep learning model that comprises multiple LSTM layers, dropout layers to prevent overfitting, and a dense output layer to create melodies and forecast their commercial success. Results: Performance evaluation using accuracy, precision, recall, F1- score, and Matthew’s correlation coefficient (MCC) provides better results with the GenAI Melody-LSTM algorithm, with 89.7% accuracy, 87.5% precision, 88.2% recall, an F1-score of 87.8%, and an MCC of 0.82. Conclusion: This research demonstrates that integrating generative AI, optimal feature selection, and deep learning significantly enhances Chinese pop music compositions. The LSTM-based model generates melodies and predicts their commercial viability, enabling composers to fine-tune AI-generated music for improved quality and market appeal.
keywords: Chinese pop music | feature selection | Generative AI | LSTM networks | melody prediction

title: Enhanced Credit Card Fraud Detection Using Feature Engineering, Optimized XGBoost, and SHAP Explainability
abstract: Credit card fraud is an economic problem that requires efficient detection. We addressed this challenge using a publicly available, highly imbalanced dataset with features anonymized via Principal Component Analysis (PCA). We evaluate how feature engineering helps involving cyclical time encoding, log transform on transaction amounts, binning, and polynomial interactions between important PCA components that affects model performance. Multiple machine learning models (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost) were tested with varying imbalanced handling schemes, such as baseline, class weighting, and SMOTE. We highlight that engineered features, particularly in combination with SMOTE, considerably enhance the performance of the untuned ensemble models. Random Forest and XGBoost with SMOTE had the highest scores. After tuning, the optimal combination, XGBoost with scale-pos-weight and engineered features, obtained an AUPRC of 0.8826 and a recall of 0.8469. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis indicated that interaction terms between PCA components were top predictors, providing transparency independent of anonymization. These results highlight the benefits of feature engineering, model calibration, and explainability methods in achieving improved fraud detection in imbalanced real-world data.
keywords: Anomaly Detection | Credit card fraud detection | Explainable AI (XAI) | feature engineering | Fi...

title: MACHINE LEARNING AND NLP IN ASSESSING TERRITORIAL DIFFERENCES IN SOCIAL WELL-BEING: A COMBINED ANALYSIS OF SURVEY DATA AND VKONTAK TE DIGITAL TR ACES
abstract: This article uses a combined analysis of survey data and VKontakte digital traces to examine territorial differences in the social well-being of St. Petersburg residents. Employing the sociology of emotions as its analytical framework, the study uses machine learning and natural language processing (NLP) methods as its core instruments. Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) was used to identify key domains of urban everyday life, and an ensemble of sentiment-analysis models classified over half a million comments into five basic emotional categories. The survey data captured subjective evaluations of the urban environment and residents’ emotional reactions, while the digital traces revealed situational and collective forms of emotional expression. The findings show that differences in social well-being consistently emerge at the intersection of district-specific infrastructure, housing quality, demographic structure and everyday mobility patterns. Social media data refine and extend insights from surveys by revealing localised points of tension, such as infrastructure failures, 'growing pains' in rapidly developing districts, and chronic everyday inconveniences characteristic of older neighbourhoods. The study demonstrates that combining survey methods with AI-based text analysis enables social well-being to be viewed as a dynamic process sensitive to changes in the urban environment, rather than a static indicator. The results have practical implications for urban social policy and for diagnosing territorial inequalities.
keywords: digital traces | machine learning | sentiment analysis (NLP) | social well-being | urban environment

title: AI-based Visualization and Quantitative Analysis of Gayageum Sanjo Vibrato Using CREPE and FFT for Traditional Korean Music Education
abstract: This study aimed to establish reference criteria for learners and performers by defining nonghyun—a core expressive element in Korean traditional music—within rhythmic sobak units. Using deep learning-based analysis with pitch extraction (CREPE) and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), gayageum sanjo performances were analyzed and visualized. Within clearly periodic rhythmic units, nonghyun segments were identified and measured in pitch, depth, speed, and frequency. The analysis showed that Jinyangjo exhibited about three nonghyun per beat and Jungmori about two, maintaining rhythmic periodicity despite tonal or phrasing variations. Future research should refine segmentation criteria and extend to diverse sanjo repertoires and performers.
keywords: deep-learning-based pitch estimation | FFT-based visualization | gayageum sanjo | Gugak education...

title: Music audio emotion regression using the fusion of convolutional neural networks and bidirectional long short-term memory models
abstract: Music emotion regression (MER) is a vital field that bridges psychology and music information retrieval. Music has the powerful ability to evoke a wide range of human emotions, from joy and sadness to anger and calmness. Understanding how music influences emotional states is essential for grasping its psychological effects on individuals. This research presents an innovative model that combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) networks to analyze and predict the emotional impact of musical audio. The model uses CNNs to detect temporal patterns and BiLSTMs to interpret sequences in both forward and backward directions, enhancing its ability to capture the complex structure of musical data. Additionally, a multi-head attention mechanism is incorporated to improve the model’s expressiveness and generalizability, making it especially effective for handling intricate sequential tasks and large datasets. The model’s performance was evaluated through sentiment prediction using extensive, publicly available datasets comprising over 9, 000 musical excerpts. Results show that the proposed model significantly outperforms existing methods in MER, achieving an R-squared value of 0.845, indicating an excellent fit with the empirical data.
keywords: Algorithms and Analysis of Algorithms | BiLSTM | CNN | Data Mining and Machine Learning | Music e...

title: Multi-Scale CNN-Based Lung Cancer Classification: Integrating Deep Learning, Texture Analysis, Bayesian Optimization and Ensemble Learning for Enhanced Diagnostic Accuracy
abstract: A proper classification system of lung cancer stands vital for early-stage diagnosis along with therapy planning. This research presents a combination of multi-scale Convolutional Neural Networks with feature fusion and Bayesian optimization-based feature weighting and Random Forest classification through boosting and bagging techniques for multiclass detection of lung cancer. The pre-processing stage of the methodology starts with lung CT image resizing followed by CLAHE enhancement then min-max normalization to achieve better image visualization. The deep hierarchical features extracted by a multi-scale CNN provide representation of global and local image patterns. Various texture features derive from Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM), Local Binary Pattern (LBP), and Wavelet Transform to boost classification discrimination. Bayesian optimization applies optimal weighting techniques to merge these features prior to obtaining maximum classification outcomes. A decision-making process powered by Random Forest with boosting and bagging works as the final classification step. Research testing performed on LIDC-IDRI and LUNA16 datasets showed that the proposed model outperformed deep learning structures ResNet-50, VGG-16, DenseNet-121 and EfficientNet-B0. The proposed model reaches a remarkable accuracy level of 97.8% alongside 97.1% sensitivity and 97.5% specificity and an AUC value of 0.98 which surpasses existing contemporary approaches. The model shows enhanced capability for generalization in addition to greater classification reliability than standard 3D-CNN and fusion models. This approach becomes a highly successful lung cancer detection method because multiple feature extraction scales along with texture analysis integration with ensemble learning and Bayesian optimization optimization techniques significantly improve classification output. The assessment methodology produces exact distinctions between benign along with probably benign and indeterminate and probably malignant lung nodules which helps to enhance diagnostic accuracy in clinical settings.
keywords: classification | deep learning | lung cancer | machine learning | nodule | segmentation

title: Machine Learning Approaches for Macroeconomic Forecasting: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Ensemble Methods
abstract: This paper evaluates the usefulness of machine learning techniques and combination methods in macro forecasts, emphasizing how they did across multiple indicators and forecasting periods. Conventional econometric models, such ARIMA and VAR, were contrasted with advanced machine learning approaches like as Decision Trees, Random Forests, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Neural Networks. Ensemble instruments, for instance Bagging (Random Forest), Boosting (GBM), and Stacking, were tested for their effect on prediction accuracy. The research applied multiple natural metrics-Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE)-to compare model performance. The results demonstrate that Neural Networks exceeded the background model accuracy, with the Interspersed ensemble approach displaying the most considerable gains across all criteria. The area graphs and line plots demonstrate that ensemble techniques generally exhibited increased performance, notably in lowering MAE and RMSE, and offered a more beneficial error shipment relative to individual models. Subsequent examination of forecasting horizons demonstrated that baseline models were effective for short-term predictions (1-4 quarters), although ensemble techniques had a considerable edge for long-term projections (5-8 quarters). Pie charts demonstrating error distribution within models verified the pre-eminence of ensemble techniques in decreasing prediction errors. This study underlines the importance of merging numerous predictive models via ensemble approaches to increase forecasting precision. The findings have practical significance for projections for money and decision-making, suggesting that applying contemporary machine learning and ensemble methodologies may considerably boost the reliability of macroeconomic predictions. Future work should consider supplemental hybrid models and inclusion of external inputs to boost forecasting precision.
keywords: Economic indicators | Ensemble methods | Machine learning | Macroeconomic forecasting | Predictiv...

title: Classification of Iranian classical music using a combination of simple networks
abstract: Music Information Retrieval (MIR) is a rapidly advancing field dedicated to the scientific analysis of music across different cultures. This research explores the application of an Error-Correcting Output Codes (ECOC) framework combined with a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) for the classification of Iranian classical music, an area that has been less explored in computational musicology. The novel approach leverages the NAVA dataset, a new standard in MIR specifically structured for this task, to address the challenge of distinguishing complex musical modes known as Dastgahs, which are integral to Iranian music. The proposed model reduces computational complexity while achieving higher classification accuracy compared to traditional deep learning models. This study demonstrates the potential of MLP-ECOC models to handle high feature dimensionality and various musical complexities effectively. This research contributes to the broader application of MIR technologies in non-Western musical contexts, aiming to enhance personalised music discovery and provide a deeper understanding of the cultural heritage embedded in music. This work sets a new standard in the field, promoting simpler, yet effective, ensemble learning techniques in music classification with a highest recorded accuracy of 96.32%.
keywords: computational musicology | ensemble learning techniques | Error-correcting output codes (ECOC) | ...

title: Method for building ensemble classifiers of structured and unstructured data based on a unified approach
abstract: Effectively classifying heterogeneous data, including structured and unstructured data, is essential in diverse fields such as healthcare, finance, information security, and audio content analysis. This study aims to develop a unified approach for constructing ensemble classifiers capable of handling diverse data formats within a single framework, enhancing classification accuracy and robustness. The methodology integrates feature extraction and data preprocessing techniques, transforming heterogeneous datasets to a standardized numerical format suitable for ensemble learning. Eight base classifiers including K-nearest neighbors, support vector machines, random forest, extreme gradient boosting, logistic regression, multilayer perception, convolution neural networks and long short-term memory networks–were trained with optimized hyperparameters. The ensemble classification uses stacking with various aggregation types such as hard voting, soft voting, and soft voting using Gompertz fuzzy ranking to effectively combine model predictions while accounting for uncertainty and noise. Experimental evaluation across five datasets, covering medical diagnosis, credit risk, emotion recognition, music genres and deepfake detection–demonstrates consistent improvement in accuracy and F1-score metrics, with gains up to 8 percent compared to the best individual classifiers. The approach proves particularly effective for unstructured audio data, where temporal and spectral dependencies pose significant challenges. The results underscore the versatility the proposed unified ensemble methodology in addressing class imbalance and noise offering a scalable solution adaptable to various domains. This work contributes a comprehensive framework facilitating the development of robust classifiers for complex real-world data and paves the way for future research integrating heterogeneous data sources within cohesive predictive models.
keywords: Ensemble classifiers | Gompertz function | hard voting | machine learning | soft voting

title: Analysis of hybrid application of neural network algorithms and expert rules for detecting anomaly condition of turbine units
abstract: Reliable and early detection of turbine unit faults is an important task to improve the reliability of power generation, especially today, when the demand for electricity is increasing. The predictive diagnostics system is proposed as a decision-making tool for identifying faults at an early stage and predicting their occurrence and progression. The study presents one of the system functions using a hybrid approach to anomaly detection and localization (FDD), based on statistical signal modeling, expert rules and probabilistic classifiers. This approach is based on the principles of ensemble learning of basic regression models, constructed using a fully connected feedforward neural network, generating diagnostic features and detecting faults through voting classifiers with weighted average probability calculations of input features, and forming a decision rule utilizing expert knowledge. The study elucidates the peculiarities and limitations in diagnostics of turbine units, approaches to the selection of predictor variables and formation of training dataset. Using this method enables for flexible and versatile tuning of algorithms and solving FDD problems under conditions of limited training dataset. The results of testing the algorithm for two instances of turbine unit journal bearing faults are presented. It is demonstrated that the proposed model enabled to identificate of the progression of an anomaly situation long well before the transgression of control threshold levels, whereas personnel and standard monitoring instruments overlooked these events.
keywords: anomaly detection | machine learning | neural network algorithms | Predictive diagnostics | regre...

title: COPD Detection and Classification by Analyzing Respiratory Audio Signals Using Deep Learning Models: Systematic Review
abstract: Respiratory sound analysis using deep learning has gained important attention due to the power of deep learning models in diagnosing respiratory diseases, including Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) and other anomalies. This paper provides a systematic review of different studies that address advanced deep learning approaches for pathology and anomaly classifications of COPD. The selected studies involved different models including recurrent neural networks (RNNs), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), hybrid models, and attention-based ensemble models. The results of accuracy in pathology classifications ranged between 90% and 99% which were higher than anomaly classifications that ranged between 72% and 86%, and this is due to the complexity of the anomaly detection. The results showed the strength of the models selected in the chosen studies, and the importance of selecting the right strategy with each model. However, the main challenges identified by this review are the diversity of datasets, feature extraction techniques, and preprocessing strategies, as well as the variability of model results in accuracy between different model designs.
keywords: Accuracy | Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease | Deep Learning | Feature Extraction | Neural Ne...

title: Toward Reliable Imagined-Speech Brain–Computer Interfaces: Subject-Independent Electroencephalogram Classification Using a Rational-Dilation Wavelet Transform and Ensemble Learning
abstract: Classifying imagined speech from electroencephalographic signals remains a significant challenge in brain–computer interface research due to the low amplitude, nonstationary properties, and high intersubject variability of the neural activity involved. However, a key unresolved problem is the poor generalizability of subject-independent imagined-speech EEG classification, largely due to inadequate multiscale signal representations and suboptimal integration of feature extraction, selection, and classification. This study introduces a subject-independent classification framework that integrates multiscale signal decomposition, statistical feature selection, and ensemble classification. Specifically, Rational-Dilation Wavelet Transform is employed to achieve flexible time-frequency analysis, followed by the extraction of time-domain, energy-based, and fractal features from each subband. Statistically discriminative features are identified using one-way analysis of variance, and classification is performed using an Extreme Gradient Boosting model with automated hyperparameter tuning. Evaluated on the Thinking Out Loud dataset, a publicly available imagined speech corpus, the proposed pipeline achieved a subject-independent test set accuracy of 64.45%, substantially outperforming prior methods that typically reported accuracies between 25.8% and 33.9%. The cross-validation results closely matched the performance of the test set, indicating a strong generalization. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of signal-aware decomposition and statistically principled feature engineering in improving the robustness of imagined speech classification. The proposed approach provides a promising basis for future developments in noninvasive neural decoding and silent communication BCIs.
keywords: BCI | brain–computer interfaces | classification | EEG | electroencephalogram | imagined speech |...

title: Discerning Music Genres: Exploring Neural Network Architectures for Automated Classification
abstract: This study investigates the application of various artificial neural network (ANN) architectures for music genre classification, focusing on the evolution of models and their performance on the GTZAN dataset. Through experimentation with fully connected networks, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and Transformer-based architectures, we analyze their strengths and limitations in genre classification. The results demonstrate that hyperparameter tuning, dataset diversity, and model selection significantly impact classification performance. Although CNNs, RNNs, and gated recurrent units (GRUs) achieve more precision than 90% in evaluation tests, the addition of Transformer layers does not consistently improve classification accuracy and may exacerbate challenges in certain genres. These results underscore the importance of carefully considering model architecture and dataset characteristics in music genre classification. Future research should focus on developing extensive, multi-rater verified datasets to enhance classification performance and model robustness in music genre classification tasks.
keywords: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) | Feature Extraction | Hyperparameter Tuning | Machine Learn...

title: Ensemble Learning with Confidence-Based Rejection for Equitable Skin Disease Diagnosis Across Skin Tones
abstract: Skin diseases are among the most widely encountered yet avoidable conditions globally. Despite their prevalence, however, it is challenging to diagnose them properly because of factors of color change in the skin, hairiness, and occlusions that obscure visual signs. Early diagnosis is crucial to allow for proper treatment, which previously relied on specialist expertise from dermatologists. Developments in recent artificial intelligence, combined with expanding access to clinical image data, however, now allow for the development of more advanced, automatic diagnosis systems. This paper introduces the development of an ensemble deep learning model for the classification of the five common skin diseases: Basal Cell Carcinoma, Eczema, Melanocytic Nevi, Seborrheic Keratosis, and Verruca Vulgaris. Three convolutional neural networks, DenseNet121, EfficientNetB0, and MobileNetV3, are utilized as the backbone of the system. Several voting strategies, including soft voting and hard voting (equal and weighted), are investigated to enhance the diagnostic precision. A confidence thresholding mechanism is also introduced to filter out uncertain predictions. Data has been obtained from PADUFES-20, Stanford AIMI, and DermNet to provide an adequate representation of skin colors. Preprocessing for images involves the use of methods such as rotation, flipping, contrast and brightness, zoom, and noise addition. The model presented has striking classification accuracy and fairness, meaning that it may be used as an auxiliary instrument for dermatology diagnosis in real-world applications.
keywords: AI | Bias Reduction | CNN | Deep Learning | Ensemble Learning | Medical Imaging | Skin Disease

title: Hybrid Generative Memory Networks for Efficient Dance Movement Generation and Classification
abstract: Dance movement generation using deep learning algorithms seeks to automate the creation of choreography, yet current models often produce movements that lack musicality, stylistic consistency, and natural human biomechanical flow. Traditional methods of generating the dance models have several bottlenecks, such as limited creativity, non-adaptability, non-scalable, and non-synchronization with the music. To overcome these challenges, this article proposes a novel ensemble of residual low-complexity Sparse Gated Networks with the Style2GAN to learn the feature dependencies between the music and realistic dance, which aids in the better classification and identification of dance steps. The proposed framework employs Style2GAN for better dance movement generation. The framework employs a novel Sparse Gated recurrent units for the extraction of temporal features that aids for the better classification of dance movements in accordance to the music style. The suggested ensemble model is trained with Kaggle's dance datasets and compared with the other traditional learning algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate that the suggested model has achieved an accuracy of 0.99, precision of 0.989, and recall of 0.987, respectively. This research sheds brighter light of research on deep learning for dance movement classification.
keywords: dance generation movement | natural biomechanical flow | sparse low-complexity gated networks | s...

title: An Intelligent Music Teaching System Based on Lite Models and Android Platform
abstract: With the increasing demand for mobile and personalized education, the integration of music teaching with intelligent mobile platforms has become a crucial direction for innovation in modern education. This paper presents the design and development of a Music Teaching System based on the Android platform, aimed at providing an interactive, portable, and scalable solution for students and educators. The system architecture follows the B/S model and is developed using Java and Kotlin for Android Studio. It integrates core modules including music theory tutorials, instrument practice guidance, AI-based voice and pitch recognition, real-time feedback, and student performance analytics. A lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is embedded to evaluate pitch accuracy and rhythm synchronization in real-time during singing or instrument practice. The system was tested by 150 music learners over a period of 4 weeks. Results indicate a significant improvement in learning engagement (by 35%) and accuracy in pitch recognition (by 28%) compared to traditional app-less teaching approaches. The application also supports offline content access and cloud-based progress synchronization, making it suitable for both urban and rural learning contexts.
keywords: android application | CNN | intelligent teaching system | mobile learning | music education | pit...

title: TuFoC: regional classification of Turkish folk music recordings using deep learning on Mel spectrograms
abstract: The regional classification of Turkish folk music remains a relatively unexplored domain in music information retrieval, particularly when leveraging raw audio signals for deep learning. This study addresses this gap by investigating how modern deep learning architectures can effectively classify regional folk recordings from limited original data using carefully designed spectrogram inputs. To address this challenge, we present Turkish Folk Music Classification (TuFoC), a deep learning-based approach that classifies Turkish folk music recordings according to their region of origin using Mel spectrogram representations. We investigate two complementary architectures: a MobileNetV2-based convolutional neural network (CNN) for extracting spatial representations, and a long short-term memory (LSTM) network for modeling temporal dynamics. To engage critically with the state of the art, we replicate a classical machine learning pipeline that combines histogram of oriented gradients (HOG) features with a Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LightGBM) classifier and Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE)-based oversampling. This baseline achieves competitive results, particularly on GAD, with 92.53% accuracy and macro F1-score. However, our CNN architecture not only marginally outperforms the baseline on the gently augmented dataset (GAD) (92.68% accuracy) but also demonstrates superior consistency across all dataset variants. While the LSTM model underperforms on original dataset (OD) and strongly augmented dataset (AD), it improves markedly on GAD, validating the importance of balanced data preparation.
